long_description:
[Kirtan Tickets at TUA](https://summerfunkirtan.eventbrite.com)

Join us for an evening of high bhakti-yoga vibrations as we chant the ancient mantras and divine names. Kirtan is like a spiritual sing-along (mostly call & response) that opens the heart, calms the mind and allows your soul to sing!
You do not have to be a singer to participate; this is a vibrational, sound-healing practice. You are welcome to sing, dance or just sit quietly and absorb the powerful vibrations. Like all practices of Yoga, Kirtan helps to dissolve the layers of all that we are not so we can perceive the true beauty of our soul.
Bring your water bottle and a few friends...The more voices, the more powerful our practice becomes as we chant for the benefit of all beings everywhere.

Dana's powerfully soulful voice will guide you deep into the practice. Her mostly Western, contemporary style of music will feel familiar even if the mantras are new to you.

Register at: [Kirtan Tickets at TUA](https://summerfunkirtan.eventbrite.com)
Please note that registering on MeetUp does not save your spot.
Energy Exchange: $15 for TUA members/$25 for non-members
Walk-ins welcome. No one gets turned away for lack of funds.

long_description:
## Rest Deeply. Heal Completely. Wake Up Restored.

Experience the profound healing power of **Yoga Nidra** \- the ancient practice of conscious relaxation also known as yogic sleep\. In this guided session with Kara\, you will be led into a deeply restful state between waking and sleeping\, where the body heals\, the mind quiets\, and the spirit renews\.

### What You Will Experience

* **Deep Physical Rest** \- Yoga Nidra is said to provide the equivalent of several hours of sleep in a single session
* **Mental Clarity** \- Release mental chatter\, stress\, and tension as you drop into a state of effortless awareness
* **Emotional Healing** \- Access deeper layers of the subconscious to release stored emotions and patterns
* **Guided by Kara** \- A warm\, experienced guide who holds space for your healing journey with care and intention

Whether you struggle with sleep, stress, or simply need a reset, this Yoga Nidra session offers a sanctuary of deep rest and renewal.

### Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: What is Yoga Nidra?**
A: Yoga Nidra, or yogic sleep, is a guided meditation practice that brings you into a deeply relaxed state between waking and sleeping. It is used for stress relief, sleep improvement, emotional healing, and spiritual development.
**Q: Do I need any experience with yoga or meditation?**
A: No experience is needed. Yoga Nidra is accessible to everyone. You simply lie down, close your eyes, and follow Kara's gentle guidance.
**Q: How long is the session?**
A: Please refer to the session details for the exact duration. Yoga Nidra sessions typically range from 20 to 60 minutes.
**Q: Is this a digital or in-person session?**
A: Please refer to the product details or contact us to confirm the session format.

long_description:
## **Urban Reset La Dera Park: Walking Meditation & Movement**

**Hosted by Monique Marie \| The Free Spirit Yogi**

### **From "Doing" into "Being"**

In the heart of the city lies a pocket of peace. Join us at **Ladera Park** for an intimate, guided journey designed to help you shed the noise of the week and return to your center. This isn't just a yoga class; it’s a curated experience of stillness, nature, and community.

### **The Experience**

Our reset is divided into four intentional phases:

* **The Silent Walk (40 Minutes):** We begin at our meeting spot with a single chime of the singing bowl. You will receive a **Mindful Focus Card**—a tactile, hand-held guide to anchor your thoughts as you wander toward the oaks. Every few minutes, the chime will ring again, calling you to take one deep, conscious breath, notice exactly where you are, and continue your journey in silence.
* **The Movement (35 Minutes):** Once we reach the dappled shade of the oak grove, we transition from the internal journey to the physical. We will move through a grounding yoga flow designed to integrate the peace of your walk into your body.
* **The Integration (5 Minutes):** We conclude our journey by bringing the stillness of the park into the center of our being. As we settle into our final resting pose, the "doing" is officially done. This is your time to absorb the frequency of the trees, the rhythm of your breath, and the shift in your energy.
* The play. Lets challenge our balance by trying arm balances, inversions and new asanas to deepen our practice.
* The departure. One final collective breath to share gratitude.

### **What’s Provided**

To ensure you can remain fully "hands-free" and present, we provide:

* **Yoga Mat Backpacks:** To ensure you can fully immerse yourself in the walking meditation, we provide complimentary use of our Yoga Mat Backpacks for the duration of the experience.
* **Mindful Focus Cards:** Yours to use during the event.

long_description:
**Join us for a soulful evening of live kirtan, meditation, and community.**

Bhakti Lounge Bay Area is delighted to welcome **His Grace Govinda Das**, an internationally respected kirtan practitioner who has dedicated over three decades to the practice and sharing of sacred mantra meditation.

Originally from Budapest, Hungary, Govinda Das has spent much of his life immersed in the devotional traditions of Vrindavan, India—one of the world's most revered centers of Bhakti Yoga. There, he served for many years in the renowned **24-Hour Kirtan**, a continuous offering of sacred music and meditation that has inspired seekers from around the globe.

Today, Govinda Das travels internationally, leading immersive kirtan experiences and sharing practical wisdom on the transformative power of mantra meditation. His heartfelt, meditative style invites participants—whether experienced or completely new—to experience stillness, joy, and a deeper connection through the ancient practice of chanting.

Whether you're exploring mantra meditation for the first time or have been practicing for years, this is a beautiful opportunity to immerse yourself in uplifting music, meaningful community, and an evening of inner renewal.

* Start the evening with a conscious, heartwarming vegan dinner—a perfect opportunity to meet and connect with fellow seekers and yogis.
* Then, immerse yourself in a soulful mantra meditation session with our special guest Govinda das.

***

### **Event Details**

**When:**
**6:00 PM - 6:45 PM** – Nourishing Vegan Dinner
**6:45 PM - 8:00 PM** – Mantra Meditation & Kirtan
**8:00 PM** – Closing & Fellowship

**Where:**
**Bhakti Lounge Bay Area**
135 Willow Rd, Menlo Park

Come experience an evening of soulful connection, music, and mindful nourishment. We can’t wait to welcome you!

This session is an invitation to imagine a different way of living—one where love is not simply something we feel, but the foundation from which we create our lives. As we become more aware of what we genuinely love, we gain the opportunity to intentionally design lives that reflect what matters most.

long_description:
This is unaffiliated but a free (donation-based) class that I’ve enjoyed so figured I’d post the info for anyone interested in joining in! The space is very attuned for meditation and spiritual practice. Again, I’m just a fellow student!

From their website:

Experience the Unique Power of Himalayan Yoga

As taught by the yogis from the Himalayas— Himalayan Yoga combines gentle postures, breathwork, and mindful relaxation techniques to connect body, mind, and spirit resulting in healing from within. Whether you’re new or experienced, this practice will leave you feeling relaxed, focused, and rejuvenated.

Benefits of Himalayan Yoga:

🌿 Enhanced flexibility, balance, and holistic strength
🌿 Tools/Techniques to cope with stress, anxiety and bring mental clarity
🌿 Energizing breathwork to uplift and restore overall health

💲 Pricing: Heartfelt donations ($10 suggested or pay what your heart desires and what you can…). All donations will go to support The Meditation Center.

📍 Location, parking & other essentials: The Meditation Center (TMC), 631 University Avenue NE, Minneapolis, MN 55413. Free parking is available across the street from TMC in the Church’s parking lot. Bring a water bottle. Yoga mat, pillows and blankets provided. Please arrive 5 minutes early and get comfortable in “the Hall of Tradition” on the main floor. No registration needed.

About Your Instructor:

Sunita Bhardwaj Gangopadhyay brings 18 years of affiliation in the Himalayan Yoga and meditation tradition. She has completed a 200-hour Teacher Training Program with Himalayan Yoga. Dedicated to helping students find balance and peace, Sunita focuses on making each class accessible and rewarding, regardless of experience level. Sunita has a PhD in Physics and a retired executive who worked in high tech industry for 25 years. She is currently the president of the Board at The Meditation Center. Native of India, Sunita currently lives in Eden Prairie, MN. She is married with two children.

long_description:
**We will meet in Study Room 2 near the back of the library**

**Feeling isolated or navigating the tender terrain after a relationship ends? You are not alone.** **Join us for** **Quiet Conversations: Our Haven for Connection****, a warm and welcoming space designed for genuine support and understanding.**

**We gather bi-weekly at the Glendale Branch Library. This isn't just a meetup; it's a place to find your footing, share your journey, and build meaningful connections with others who truly understand.**

**Whether you're newly separated, years post-divorce, or simply looking to expand your supportive circle, this peer-led group offers a haven to feel seen, heard, and deeply supported.** **Please note: This is a peer-led community, not a therapy or coaching group. It's a space for shared experience and mutual encouragement, not professional mental health support.**

**Your Contribution to Our Haven:** **This community thrives on the spirit of mutual support. Many members have expressed how invaluable these gatherings are, and some have even offered to contribute financially. To help us continue providing this vital space and cover Meetup fees and other community resources, we welcome your support.**

**Suggested Donation: $10 - $20 per session (or whatever feels right for you).** **Your generosity helps us keep things going and the conversations flowing.**

**You can contribute via Venmo: @michaelleavitthwb**

**Ready to find your chosen family?** **If you're also looking for a creative outlet and a deeper dive into music and shared creativity, check out our sister community,** **[Wandering Bards](https://www.meetup.com/wanderingbard)****. long_description:
Hey Poetry Lovers!

This group is on a roll. Here’s the gist:

We meet at the **Capital One Café in Chinatown** from **12pm - 2pm** every other week.

For enrichment, we start by reading and reflecting on a **“published poem”**, suggested by someone in the group. No advance preparation is necessary. But feel free to check out some of the poems we’ve read [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vSyE_wCLQCPHRrKmN5F9tOIeeRQUZESxjRXGVBoCF2uU8Gm0_d0uECiCBCQXEy6ksxfsBOhtRIOpW3T/pubhtml?gid=0&single=true&widget=true&headers=false%22%3E%3C/iframe%3E). Or submit suggestions for future meetings [here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSexGc2Z2Kp6bZW0D3_hfJ7NUUkfNHf7TXX-43FglCeBd9EF2Q/viewform?usp=send_form).

Next, we **share our work and offer feedback**. Depending on attendance, everyone gets \~10 minutes to use as they like. (No need to share, though; you’re welcome to come even if you prefer just to listen.)

We maintain a **Discord server** to help share our work and communicate outside our bi-weekly meet-ups. If you haven’t used Discord before, take a moment to download it and create an account before arriving. When we meet you on Saturday, we will add you to our server, the “DC Poetry Workshop”, and can help you navigate the app if you have questions.

Finally, if you plan on sharing a poem, consider how you will do so. Some options include:

* Print 5-10 copies to distribute in person
* Take and share screenshots in the Discord chat.
* Copy the poem into a google doc, change sharing settings to “anyone with link”, and copy the google doc link into the Discord chat.

Most importantly, we’re excited to meet you!

Catch you on Saturday,

Diego / Ian / Cayden / Nate / Otasha / Lia / An

long_description:
We get it -- yoga can seem intimidating especially when you see photos of yogis with their heels behind their necks. Relax, in this class we cater to the new or hesitant yogi. The postures are simple with props available (think of training wheels on a bicycle) to make them easy to express. Simple but very nourishing. We believe yoga is 4 every body, not just for the young and naturally flexible.

Yoga is a way to get to know our bodies better, calm our ever-thinking minds and enjoy some inner peace. Treat yourself to 90 minutes self-care. Leave class refreshed and rejuvenated! Feel free to leave questions in the comments section or message me on meetup.

Class includes breath-work, postures, correct alignment, relaxation, meditation, and yogic wisdom. Modifications to postures are suggested to accommodate individual needs.

Our bodies are unique so beginners are encouraged to take their time and adapt slowly to the postures, resting as they deem appropriate for their bodies. Props such as chairs, blocks, straps, bolsters and blankets are available in studio to assist you.

Yoga is a practice that cultivates joy, concentration, mindfulness, body awareness, flexibility, health and serenity. Simply put, yoga is fun. It is not a sequence of masochistic exercises!

This does not mean we practice yoga haphazardly. Quite the contrary. We bring body, breath, mental focus and magnanimous spirit to every asana (posture.) We are fully present . . . but without strain, tension, self-judgment or perfectionism.

My name is Frank . I am a certified 200-hour Registered Yoga Teacher with the Yoga Alliance. I am experienced in working with men who have survived trauma and are thriving. I am a recovering workaholic / aka Type A personality. Through the blessings of yoga I have a personal practice that integrates health of my body with peace of mind and deepens my connection to That which Is. I am honored to share yoga with you. Namaste!

45 South Main Street, Suite 90 SunDo Wellness.

long_description:
Ongoing training and study of the "Arte e Scientia d'Armizare" ("Art & Science of Armed Fighting") of Italian medieval fight-master Fiore dei Liberi. Yes, the medieval Europeans had their own martial art systems!

ARTE E SCIENTIA D'ARMIZARE

Using medieval manuscripts we are studying and practicing what European professional soldiers (mercenaries) and nobles learned about mortal combat 600 years ago in northern Italy, from fightmaster Fiore dei Liberi. The Arte e Scientia d'Armizare, which survives today in the form of several manuscripts in museums, includes hand to hand combat/grappling, dagger fighting, longsword fighting and fighting with a seven foot spear.

Your "Istruttore" (Instructor) in Fiore's Arte e Scientia d'Armizare is Colin Hatcher, a martial artist of 40 years, beginning in 1977, with over 30 years as an instructor. In addition to a long history with the Eastern martial arts Colin has also been studying and teaching the Historical European Martial Arts (known as "HEMA") for 20 years.

This meet-up is run by historical European martial arts (HEMA) school "Accademia del Leone" ("The Academy of the Lion"), founded in 2014.

No prior knowledge or skill is required. You will find us a welcoming group and safety is a priority. Please wear comfortable clothing and don't forget to bring water to keep hydrated.

long_description:
Within each of us lies a dream that carries us toward Africa. Whether it began in childhood or later in life, the image of the savanna, snow-capped mountains, and untamed wildlife stirs curiosity, emotion, and the desire for adventure. Kilimanjaro, the rooftop of the African continent, is the symbol of that call — a legendary mountain, a natural wonder that seems lifted from an African fairytale. With its imposing silhouette surrounded by tropical forests and arid savannas, Kilimanjaro offers a one-of-a-kind experience — a journey from equatorial jungle to a landscape resembling the polar tundra.

It's an ascent that leaves a mark not only physically but emotionally. As you climb, you don't just reach a summit — you rediscover a part of yourself. The peak offers a new horizon: clearer, broader, and more confident.

From a technical standpoint, Kilimanjaro is the most accessible peak of the famous Seven Summits and Seven Volcanoes. It doesn't require mountaineering skills and is successfully climbed each year by people of all ages — from 6 to 83 years old. The trails are well-maintained, logistics are excellent, and porters carry most of the gear, making the experience both comfortable and achievable.

For those who want to extend their African journey, the expedition can be followed by a spectacular safari in Tarangire and Ngorongoro — the land of great migrations, lions, and elephants, an unmatched natural spectacle.

This is more than just a vacation — it's a journey that leaves a deep mark on your soul and gently changes the way you see the world.

Highlights:
• Uhuru Peak (5,895m) – Roof of Africa
• Journey from tropical rainforest to arctic-alpine zone
• Machame Route – one of the most scenic paths
• Sunrise summit attempt under a star-filled sky
• Certificate of achievement upon completion
• Optional: Safari extension in Tarangire and Ngorongoro Crater

long_description:
Socrates Cafés are gatherings around the world where people from different backgrounds get together and exchange thoughtful ideas and experiences while embracing the Socratic Method; the idea that we learn more when we question, and question with others.
Although this may be considered a "philosophical" group, there are no rules as to what is discussed. Those attending decide upon the questions of the night. Usually, the topics revolve around social concerns, moral issues, and the first principles of things.

Prior to each meeting we vote online for the questions we will discuss. That way, we will have enough time to ruminate on them and have more in-depth conversations. If you RSVP to a meeting, you may post your question in the event comments section below. I'll send out a survey for voting a few days prior to the meetup. We discuss two questions each night. So you will get to cast two votes in the survey.
When we meet, we break into smaller groups of five to seven to discuss the top two vote-getters. Each group discusses one question for around 45-50 minutes, and we then take a short break. After reconvening, each group moves on to its second question.

Hope to see you there!

-Brian

long_description:
It’s summer and what would the season be without laughter, food and some wonderful friends? Let’s meetup in July, enjoy our beautiful Cheyenne weather and have a picnic at Holliday Park! It will be our only get together for the month so let’s make it a fun one. Here are some Q&As:

\*\* **Do I bring chairs and blankets? *Yes*.** Bring them *just in case*. It’s a small shelter and you can set up under the shade with a chair and a blanket if necessary.
\*\* **Is this a potluck? *No***. Bring something to eat and some drinks. If you don’t have a cooler, Eric and I will bring a large one just in case your stuff needs a home.
\*\* **Is there a grill at our shelter? *Yes*.** Eric and I will bring charcoal and lighter fluid in the event that any of you would like to grill something to eat.
\*\* **Will there be games? *ABSOLUTELY*!** I always have something silly planned. They’ll start at 12:30 but only for those who want to play.
\*\* **How can I find you? *EASY*!** We’ll be in a small shelter at the very northeast corner of the park. I’ll have yellow balloons to help identify where we’ll be and parking will be on the street.
\*\* **What happens if it rains? *BUMMER***! If the weather calls for scattered showers, we’ll huddle under our tiny shelter roof until the cloud passes. If the forecast calls for over a 80% chance of rain, it will be postponed until sometime in September. Just keep an eye on this page for weather updates.

And, on a final note, please remember to RSVP and send me a dm on how many children (if any) and their ages if you plan on bringing family or friends. Let me know if you have any additional questions.
I’m looking forward to the picnic, my friends. This promises to be another fun one. See you soon!!

**🚀 New for this month's meetup: The I-Framework**
Ever have a startup idea and not know what to actually build first? I've been working on a tool for exactly that, and I want you to break it before Saturday.
**The I-Framework** is a Claude Code plugin that walks you through the first three "I's" of a startup — **Intent → Ideation → Innovation** — and spits out a build-ready product spec. The core idea: *a startup is a stack of risks, and you retire them cheapest-and-most-fatal first.* Each stag
long_description:
**🚀 New for this month's meetup: The I-Framework**
Ever have a startup idea and not know what to actually build first? I've been working on a tool for exactly that, and I want you to break it before Saturday.
**The I-Framework** is a Claude Code plugin that walks you through the first three "I's" of a startup — **Intent → Ideation → Innovation** — and spits out a build-ready product spec. The core idea: *a startup is a stack of risks, and you retire them cheapest-and-most-fatal first.* Each stage kills one risk (Do people have this problem? Is this the right solution? Why do we win?) and writes one artifact to a `Product/` folder. You end up with a ranked set of feature files — each with a user story, testable acceptance criteria, and an honest **"is this our edge, or just table-stakes?"** classification. The 4th I, Implementation, is where your build team picks it up.
It's conversational — it interviews you one question at a time and pushes back on thin answers rather than just flattering the idea.
**Try it before Saturday:**

1. Have [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) installed.
2. `git clone https://github.com/InSciCo/i-framework`
3. Open the folder in Claude Code and type `/iflow` to start (or `/intent` to jump straight in). The skills auto-load — no setup.

There are four worked sample specs in `_sandbox/samples/` (meal-planning, dev tooling, a marketplace, fintech) if you want to see the output first.
Run it on a real idea of yours, bring what it produced — or where it fell over — and we'll dig into it together Saturday.

Hosted by Yulia Denisyuk, a veteran [travel journalist](https://www.yulia-denisyuk.com/), host of the [Going Places platform](https://goingplacesmedia.com/), and teacher who's traveled to over 100 countries in search of wisdom. During a women's circle at the Temple of Moon in Peru, Yulia felt the call to continue these gatherings back home – and she followed the call.

This is not a yoga session. This is a gathering for women to practice gentle meditation, mindfulness, stretching, and a few yoga poses meant to activate our intuition and inner wisdom.

Practical info:
\- The session will last about 1 hour\, with about 10 minutes before and after to prep and wind down\. Total time: \~ 1 hour and 10 minutes
\- Bring your own yoga mat or a blanket to sit on\.
\- The session will be on the shore of Lake Michigan in Lakeview\. We'll gather in a shaded\, tree\-lined part of the shore\.

True self-defense begins long before a physical encounter.

* Develop habits that help you avoid dangerous situations whenever possible

Physical techniques are a last resort.

* Learn verbal and behavioral strategies to de-escalate conflict
* Practice maintaining calm and control under stress
* Focus on creating safe exits whenever possible

***

Build strong fundamentals that protect your body.

* Learn safe, balanced fighting and defensive stances
* Understand how positioning improves stability and awareness
* Practice movement that reduces injury risk

* Practice locks and takedowns focused on control and escape

long_description:
**Ruidoso - Eagle Creek Trail at Alto Lakes July 18th - 9am - noon**

**Sign up at: https://www.riograndesierraclub.org/calendar/**
Join u for a short brisk hike through the cool pines of Ruidoso. Our hike starts at the Alto Lake Parking lot & we'll take a leisurely 2 mile round trip hike along and behind Alto Lake, and we might catch a glimpse of some wild horses or elk. This trail is a[Full Description](https://campfire.sierraclub.org/campfire/apex/ClubEventEntry?id=a4SPo000005p7J7MAI#full-description)lso used by bird watchers that hosts several songbirds, ducks and hawks. The Eagle Creek Trail has a minimal elevation gain and we'll discuss a little of its hydrology.We will also discuss & view two drinking ground water wells along the trail. This area has several drinking water wells that the Water Dept. for the Village of Ruidoso uses for public consumption. We will discuss a little about the water system and how it is maintained and sent into distribution and storage. Finally we will discuss EPA Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) requirements, laws, sampling & testing, public notice issues and Consumer Confident Reporting. Limit is 8 people, no dogs. Deadline for registering is July 16th.
**Sign up at: https://www.riograndesierraclub.org/calendar/**

Intentional dating for young professionals through running.
A low-pressure, comfortable alternative for meeting other single young professionals who value staying active, building a genuine connection, and living a purposeful life.
Each run is themed and thoughtfully organized to create a welcoming environment, with sub-groups curated around shared hobbies, interests, values, or lifestyle preferences.
Expect a relaxed vibe, a balanced gender ratio, and a comfortable social setting designed to help people connect organically.
After the run, we’ll continue the social over dinner so there’s time to connect beyond the route.
Come solo or bring a friend.
We'll meet at the tall Obelisk structure in Hermann Park that's next to the Reflection Pool.
----

Feeling someone's vibe takes more than one interaction. That’s why Two Mile Dating is built around repeated, low-pressure opportunities to see familiar faces, get more comfortable, and let chemistry develop naturally.
Although we can't engineer chemistry, we stand behind the space we're creating to help you to connect with others: attend six consecutive runs and if you don't connect with anyone, your next six runs are on us.

Ankati Day is a yoga teacher, ceremonialist, DJ, and sound healer who has been guiding transformative experiences since 2012. Her work blends mindfulness, music, and embodied awareness to create spaces where people can reconnect with themselves, release stress, and cultivate a deeper sense of presence.

Ankati’s sessions are known for being both grounding and deeply restorative, offering a gentle invitation to slow down, listen inward, and return to the heart.

long_description:
**Q: What is this “Great Films Project” thing?**
A: It’s an opportunity for in-depth conversation about the greatest films ever made. Each month, we’ll be discussing and analyzing three acclaimed films. This July those films will be "8&1/2", "Sunrise: A Song of Two Humans", and "The Searchers").

**Q: How is this different than your regular monthly topic-driven Meetups?**
A: Think of it a little more like a book club. We want to do deep dives into these films and may spend an hour or more dissecting each one (which is why we’re limiting to three). Because we want to truly engage with these films, we’re asking that all attendees come in familiar with them and have strong opinions, stimulating questions and enthusiasm to engage and discover.

**Q: Hold on! Who’s to say what the “greatest films ever made” are? Isn’t that subjective?**
A: Of course, and opinions on why a film should or should not be considered such will be very up for discussion. But there has long been and evolving “film canon” set over the years by critics, film scholars and cinephiles. We are using the Top 1,000 Greatest Films list from the “They Shoot Pictures, Don't They?” website ([https://theyshootpictures.com/](https://theyshootpictures.com/))

**Q: So, what’s so great about this list?**
A: It's not just one list. It’s an annual aggregation of "best-of" film lists from almost 11,000 individual lists by critics, filmmakers, publications, and websites. TSPDT is critic-driven. It prioritizes historical influence, artistic innovation, and critical consensus. That doesn’t mean we will all agree with the rankings, but we think it’s a good place to start.

**Q: What movies are coming up? What will this monthly “project” look like over time?**
A: That’s an easy one. Just go to the TSPDT top 1,000 list ([https://theyshootpictures.com/gf1000_all1000films_table.php](https://theyshootpictures.com/gf1000_all1000films_table.php)) and check out the first 36 titles. Those are the films we’ll cover over a year,

long_description:
RSVP's close Saturday's at 6pm.

**Why A Men’s Yoga Class?**

Standard yoga classes may be a little intimidating for men because we are not reared to be physically flexible. Practicing yoga together allows men to be part of a team in a non-competitive way and this nourishes our ancient gravitation towards a tribe of warriors.

Working together towards common goals of increased flexibility, body awareness, health, inner peace, self-confidence, or spiritual development creates powerful motivational energy enabling us to reach new heights. Consider the drafting effect of a flock of wild geese or the magnified success ratio of two lions hunting together. The positive male vibes carry through our week enhancing our personal and work relationships and our sense of purpose/mission in life.

**Benefits of Yoga:**

\-\- \> Increases flexibility

--> Improves posture

--> Tones muscles

--> Improves overall health and well-being

--> Reduces effects of stress

--> Promotes relaxation

-->Fosters peace of mind

--> Deepens spiritual connections

Through regular practice of yoga we improve our range of motion which complements our athletic performance in sports and reduces the likelihood of sports-related injuries.

More subtly, yoga enhances our body awareness and we become more attuned to our body’s signals for spontaneous stretching, posture corrections and rest and relaxation.

These benefits of yoga are available to everyone from the beginner to the more experienced practitioner.

**What’s Special About Men’s Yoga?**

Men generally tend to hold stress and tension in the shoulders and back, and are often tight in the hips, groin and hamstrings. So we focus on loosening muscles in these areas. Additionally we focus on standing postures, balance poses, and chest openers such as virabhadrasana --warrior -- to develop a confident, grounded stance and even mind to meet the many challenges the world throws at us.

long_description:
The Murfreesboro, TN Recovering From Religion support group will meet the third Sunday of every month at 3:00pm at the Technology Engagement Center, barring inclement weather or the date falls on a holiday. Attendees can remain anonymous if they so choose and are not required to tell their story if they do not wish to, but everyone will be welcomed to do so.

The primary focus of a Recovering From Religion support group is to provide ongoing and personal support to individuals as they let go of their religious beliefs. This transitional period is an ongoing process that can result in a range of emotions, as well as a ripple effect of consequences throughout an individual’s life. As such, the support meetings are safe and anonymous places to express these doubts, fears, and experiences without biased feedback or proselytizing.

We are here to help each other through this journey.

There is no cost to attend this support group but, if you feel so inclined, donations can be made at www.recoveringfromreligion.org/donate

RfR has an immense collection of well-curated resources available as you go through your journey. The page includes resources for mental and physical crises, working with relationships, for issues stemming from specific religions, coming out stories, and much more. Head to www.recoveringfromreligion.org/resources for these helpful resources.

If you find you need to talk with someone before the meeting date, RfR has a hotline and online chat for that express purpose. Call (844) 368-2848 to speak with someone or go to www.recoveringfromreligion.org to chat online.

If you are in need of professional help, we can offer the Secular Therapy Project to provide options to connect with a professional therapist. All therapists have been thoroughly vetted by our organization and offer only evidence-based and non-religious treatment. Connect with them at www.seculartherapy.org.

long_description:
### **🔥 Sunday Fire Circle — Queen's Beach Park (by Barefoot Beach Cafe)**

**Always free. Always open to watchers. No pressure, no cost — just come.**
End your weekend the way it deserves to end. We gather on the grass at Queen's Beach Park, right by Barefoot Beach Cafe, where the sun sets behind Waikiki and the ocean keeps time. Grab a coffee or a bite from Barefoot, find a soft patch of grass, and settle in.
This is O'ahu's cross-disciplinary movement arts community — fire dancers, poets, musicians, DJs, yogis, holistic facilitators, and friends. Come spin. Come share a piece. Come stretch, drum, sing, or just witness the circle come alive against the dusk.

**The Flow of the Night**

* **One hour before sunset** — Classes & skill shares. Beginner-friendly intros to poi, staff, fans, and safe spinning. Props to borrow, teachers ready.
* **Sunset** — The circle opens. Fire goes up, music comes on, the night begins. If you aren't spinning fire you are encouraged to dance to the music regardless!
* **9 PM** — Last burn. We pack out together.

**What to Bring (if you're spinning)**

* Natural fiber clothing (cotton or wool — no synthetics near flame)
* Water + a layer for after dark
* Your prop, instrument, mic, or mat
* A small light for setup and breakdown

**Just watching?** Bring yourself. Maybe a blanket. That's it.
**Before You Spin: Sign the Waiver**
Anyone stepping into the circle to spin needs to complete our waiver. Two minutes, online: **[https://www.trialbyfire.community/fire-circle](https://www.trialbyfire.community/fire-circle)**
**Community Guidelines**

* **Consent first** — ask before you touch, photograph, or enter someone's space.
* **Substance-free** — Strictly no alcohol, no cocaine, no ketamine.
* **The circle is working space** — stay outside the perimeter unless you're spinning, fueling, or on safety.
* **Respect the fuel, props, and people.**
* **Leave it better than you found it.**

**RSVP if you can — helps us plan props and safeties. New h

long_description:
Join our group for a guided meditation!

The event begins with a short introductory talk on Buddhism. This is followed by a guided Vajrayana Buddhist meditation. The meditation generally lasts \~20 minutes, and it is accessible and beneficial to people of all experience levels. You are welcome to stay afterwards to ask any questions or talk further.

We will have meditation cushions available, but you are welcome to bring your own if you like. Chairs can also be made available for those who need them.

What Is Buddhist Meditation?

In Buddhism, meditation means "effortlessly remaining in what is". This state may be brought about by calming and holding the mind, when compassion and wisdom are realized, or by working with our bodies' energy channels and meditating on light forms of Buddhas.

About Us

Diamond Way Buddhist Center Chicago belongs to an international non-profit network of over 600 lay Diamond Way Buddhist centers of the Karma Kagyu lineage of Tibetan Buddhism, founded by Lama Ole Nydahl and under the spiritual guidance of H.H. the 17th Gyalwa Karmapa, Trinley Thaye Dorje.

Diamond Way Buddhism offers practical and effective methods to realize mind’s inherent richness for the benefit of all. With an accessible and modern style, it works with people’s confidence and desire, using every situation in life to develop fearlessness and joy. We always present a basic introduction for newcomers, and the meditations are guided in English.

To learn more about our center visit:
http://www.diamondway.org/chicago/

\*This event is free. Just come as you are and enjoy.

This week long day camp is a crash course in multidisciplinary video game design. Students will team up and learn how to program 2D video games with the free and open-source Godot engine. Students will learn about the art pipeline as they hand-draw, animate, and integrate their own art assets, and even how to compose and record music for their games. The ideal candidates for this camp are high school students who are computer-savvy and creative. They have coded some before, but they may not have used Godot. They are interested in the practice of game design, and open to learning how to draw and how to compose music.

You have the opportunity to fall in love with yourself and explore the possibility of attracting a loving relationship that reflects that love.

The relationship you have with another and with yourself are themes to be discovered in this experiential and didactic therapeutic learning environment. The greatest path to learning as an adult is through experience, so as you participate in all of the workshops, you will glean more insight and skills as you manifest.

Kundalini Yoga and Meditation

Known as “The Yoga of Awareness,” Kundalini Yoga is a powerful and time-honored practice that creates rapid, lasting transformation. It’s a complete system that combines movement, conscious breathwork, meditation, and mantra to align your body, mind, and soul.

This practice doesn’t require flexibility or experience—just a willingness to show up. Whether you're holding a demanding job, raising a family, or navigating the daily pressures of modern life, Kundalini Yoga gives you practical tools to stay calm, centered, and resilient.

Each class includes dynamic exercises (kriyas), guided meditations, breathwork, chanting, and ends with a deeply relaxing Gong bath to help you unwind and integrate.

Kundalini Yoga offers results from the very first class—no prior yoga experience needed.

Benefits include:
• Builds nervous system strength and stress resilience
•Balances the brain hemispheres for mental clarity
• Lifts mood and clears emotional stagnation
• Detoxifies organs like the liver and lungs
• Strengthens and tones muscles & joints
• Increases circulation and boosts energy levels
• Improves lung capacity and oxygen flow
• Enhances intuition, awareness, and focus
• Prepares the body and mind for meditation

Themes change week to week, addressing what we experience as human beings. All levels welcome.

What to bring:
Wear comfortable clothes (white cotton is suggested for its uplifting energy, but not required).

long_description:
**THE GREAT MINGLE**
**Come Curious. Who Will You Meet?**

Looking to meet new people beyond your usual circle?

Join Tribe of One Love for **The Great Mingle**, a fun and intentionally structured social experience designed to help you connect with people you may never have met otherwise.
Many social events naturally lead us to spend time with the people we already know. ***The Great Mingle is different.***

Using a format we call **The Social Shuffle**, we'll guide participants through a series of small-group conversations designed to make meeting new people easy, comfortable, and engaging.

No awkward networking. No pressure. Just meaningful conversations with interesting humans.

Whether you're new to the community or a long-time member, you'll have the opportunity to meet a variety of people, hear their stories, share your own, and leave feeling more connected than when you arrived.

**Shared Intention**
To create opportunities for genuine human connection by stepping beyond our familiar circles, approaching one another with curiosity, and recognizing that every person carries a unique story worth discovering. And while our gatherings give us a place to start, Tribe of One Love hopes the magic doesn’t end there—may the conversations, friendships, and unexpected sparks continue to grow naturally long after the event lights dim.

**Eat Street Crossing Venue (2nd Floor, The Prince Lounge)**
Eat Street Crossing is a vibrant Minneapolis food hall featuring sushi, ramen, banh mi, tacos, Brazilian pizza, boba, ice cream, craft beer, THC cocktails, and more. It's designed as a community gathering space with multiple food vendors, a bar, communal seating, and even a self-serve tap wall.

The Prince Lounge is a special area on the second floor. If needed, take the elevator up to the event. Come early, grab dinner or a drink, and settle in on the second floor before we begin.

**Parking**
There are two parking lots where you can park for free. One is across the street on C

title: Profs & Pints DC: Designing Belonging
description:
[Profs and Pints DC](https://www.profsandpints.com/washingtondc) presents: **“Designing Belonging,”** on the messages sent by various institutional environments and how they can be made more welcoming, with Martha Kakooza, research associate in the department of higher education and student affairs at Morgan State University, where she teaches courses on gender, sexuality, and narrative and qualitative research.

[Advance tickets: $13.50 plus sales tax and processing fees. Available at [https://
long_description:
[Profs and Pints DC](https://www.profsandpints.com/washingtondc) presents: **“Designing Belonging,”** on the messages sent by various institutional environments and how they can be made more welcoming, with Martha Kakooza, research associate in the department of higher education and student affairs at Morgan State University, where she teaches courses on gender, sexuality, and narrative and qualitative research.

[Advance tickets: $13.50 plus sales tax and processing fees. Available at [https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/dc-designing-belonging](https://events.ticketleap.com/tickets/profsandpints/dc-designing-belonging) .]

Why do some rooms make people relax while others make them stiffen? Why do certain workplaces, schools, restaurants, churches, airports, and waiting rooms seem to say, “you are welcome here,” while others quietly signal “this was not built with you in mind”?

Explore how ordinary spaces shape belonging at a talk that will offer guidance to those seeking to create inclusive environments for students, clients, and customers. Being on hand will help anyone out there sort out why some environments have felt so welcoming while others left them focused on exits.

You’ll learn how a room's layout, lighting, seating, signage, sound, artwork, security presence, and history all affect whether people feel at ease or on edge, powerful or invisible, cared for or merely processed. People read these cues almost instantly, usually before they can explain why a place feels welcoming or alienating.

Dr. Martha Kakooza, a scholar whose research has focused space, identity, and institutional environments, will discuss why the same environment can feel like home to one person and like a closed door to another. She’ll describe how experiences of race, culture, class, gender, age, disability, and migration all shape how we read a space. We’ll look at how no space is truly neutral, because each one carries social messages and histories.

long_description:
This is a beginner-friendly guitar group for adults navigating life after separation or divorce who want a creative, grounding way to reconnect with themselves.

No experience required. If you’ve never played guitar—or if life interrupted your creativity—this space is designed to be gentle, supportive, and human.

**Bring your guitar** and we’ll start with basic chords, simple strumming, and learn one approachable song together each month. This isn’t about performance or perfection. This isn’t about performance or perfection. It’s about giving yourself something steady to come back to and remembering that you’re still allowed to learn, try, and enjoy things again.

I’ll be teaching the class myself, and we’ll always end with a relaxed group jam where everyone can participate at their own level.

This can be a simple standalone practice, or it can be the beginning of something deeper. Both are welcome.

**🎶 This month’s song:**
👉 "Drift Away" by Dobie Gray
👉 We will be learning the chords F, C, Dm and G

\*\*\*

### 💰 Cost & Commitment

$15 per session.
Please pay ahead via Venmo to lock in your spot. Paying ahead helps keep the group intentional.
**📲 Venmo: @michaelleavitthwb**

Prefer not to use Venmo? No problem. You can also do cash at the event, or Zelle in person.

If cost is genuinely a barrier, message me. We’ll figure something out.

### Location

We will be meeting inside a space at Terra Diamond, a local warehouse.. Come in through the front door and head up the staircase on the left. At the top of the stairs, we’ll be in the second room on your right. There’s a large window, so you should be able to spot us easily.

long_description: A long standing casual event for Christian men. (Looking to start a women’s version of this soon. Message me if interested ) Grab a cup of coffee and a donut or just take a seat. We are currently growing our ROYAL Spa Team and would love to offer opportunities for you all to apply and become a part of our amazing Royalty staff.

To apply please send resume & interests to:
Subject: Hiring Event
[PlushRoyaltyMassage@Gmail.com](mailto:PlushRoyaltyMassage@Gmail.com)

Someone from our Royalty Team will respond within 2- 3 business days, to set an appointment for the hiring event day. The Actual day of the event is where you will interview in-person, ask questions and gain understanding of the positions offered.

We are currently accepting Nevada licensed massage therapists, and student externships.

Our requirements to apply:

\- Must be at least 18 years of age

long_description:
Venmo: @shaniahann
Cost: $15.00

**From Breath to Stillness: Breathwork & Yoga Nida**

Join us for a deeply restorative journey designed to calm the nervous system, reconnect you with your body, and invite profound rest.
We begin with approximately 20 minutes of a guided three-part conscious breathing practice. This intentional breathwork helps ground you in the present moment, deepen your connection to your body, and gently release stored stress, tension, and emotions that may be ready to move. As the breath creates space within, you'll naturally transition into a state of greater openness and ease.
From there, you'll be guided into Yoga Nidra, often referred to as *yogic sleep* or *psychic sleep*—a deeply restorative meditation practiced while lying comfortably in stillness. In this state between wakefulness and sleep, the body receives profound rest while the mind remains gently aware. Yoga Nidra offers an opportunity to regulate the nervous system, cultivate inner awareness, and plant intentions that can help shift subconscious patterns and beliefs.
Whether you're feeling overwhelmed, emotionally depleted, or simply seeking a moment to slow down, this practice offers a space to release, restore, and return home to yourself. You'll leave feeling more grounded, refreshed, and deeply nourished from the inside out.
**No previous experience is necessary.** All are welcome.

Venmo: @shaniahann
Cost: $15.00

long_description:
Here's the agenda for this Meetup:

Please note we will start promptly at 12:00 pm. Please be a few minutes early so you will have time to order some lunch. Also, give yourself a few minutes to catch up with other members. This will ensure that we can start on time and then we will be able to leave on time.

We do ask that as we get back to in-person networking, you WILL NEED to buy lunch to support Rock Bottom, there will also be a $1 restaurant service fee (that is NOT part of the gratuity) added to all checks.

• We'll do a brief introduction of ABNG and also quickly go over our rules (don't worry, there's only three and a half!). Then, we'll get right to the meeting.

• Hold on to your business cards for now. We will start the meeting by going around the room with our introductions. Notice we didn't say 30-second commercial or elevator pitch. There's a fantastic TED talk (https://youtu.be/u4ZoJKF_VuA) from Simon Sinek that might blow you away.

• After introductions, we'll do our shoutouts and share our member events. If you had a great 1:1 with someone or have some other awesome thing to share, we have the space for that! If you have a workshop, class, meeting or event coming up, this is a great time to inform the group. We will also discuss specific needs you may have. Do you need a resource of some kind? Chances are someone in our group can point you in the right direction.

• If time allows, we will engage in our Mastermind discussion. If you feel like you have something in your business that is holding you back, this is time and the place to tackle it. If you have something that you need help with, make sure to let the host know before the meeting starts so that we can make time for it during our meeting. The power of the group is immense!

• We'll close out our meeting by passing around business cards and ensuring you have time to set up your 1:1's before adjourning at 1:00 p.m.

We look forward to seeing you at our next meeting!

long_description:
Join us in [Atlanta for Build an Agent Day](https://www.buildanagent.io/events/atlanta-ga) and craft your own AI agent live and in person! One day. One working AI agent, built by you.

## [Build an Agent Day - Atlanta](https://www.buildanagent.io/events/atlanta-ga)

**Walk in with a workflow you hate. Walk out with an agent that does it for you.**

Build An Agent Day is a one-day, hands-on workshop where you codify a real task from your job as a working AI agent — and leave with the design pattern to do it again and again. No slide decks to take home. By 6 PM you have something running against your own Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 account.
It's a program of [All Things AI](https://allthingsai.org/ "https://allthingsai.org") and [All Things Open](https://allthingsopen.org/ "https://allthingsopen.org"), built for the people who do the work: business professionals, government leaders, and K-12 and higher-ed educators. If you can write a clear how-to email, you can build an agent here.

#### What you'll build

Over eight hours, you'll build the same workflow across three agent stacks and pick the one that fits your environment:

* **Claude Cowork** (Anthropic) — for knowledge workers
* **ChatGPT Agents** (OpenAI) — for enterprise IT
* **Manus** — for research-heavy roles

The arc: pick a workflow you own (reports, intake, scheduling, drafting, research), capture your expertise as a skill an AI can follow, wire it into your stack, and ship it the same day. You'll demo it before you leave.

* **Crack Open the Agent** — the three primitives (model, tools, memory) and the agent loop, narrated tool call by tool call

long_description:
**U.S. - Korea Relations and the Future of South Korean Diplomatic Strategy**
The United States and the Republic of Korea share one of the most consequential partnerships in the Indo-Pacific. What began as an alliance forged in shared security commitments has matured into a broad strategic relationship spanning technology, trade, advanced manufacturing, energy, and cultural exchange. South Korea's emergence as a global leader in critical industries, democratic governance, and cultural influence has deepened this partnership's significance for both nations.

As strategic competition between the United States and China intensifies, South Korea navigates a distinct set of pressures: maintaining substantial economic ties with China while deepening its security and technology cooperation with the United States. The growing trilateral relationship among the United States, South Korea, and Japan adds another consequential dimension, offering new possibilities for regional stability while requiring careful diplomatic management. This panel brings together distinguished experts to assess the current state of the U.S.–South Korea relationship and its trajectory.

Discussion will address how regional dynamics, including the roles of China, Japan, and North Korea, are shaping the alliance, and where the two countries see the greatest opportunities and challenges ahead in trade, technology, security, and cultural exchange.

Students memorize the Ashtanga sequence at their own pace as students can adjust the practice based on their individual needs, including modification for injuries, body proportions or the energy level of a practitioner. This class has no teacher, but others in the room are available for guidance as well as to share the collective energy. Mysore is adaptable for beginners yet also offers challenges and advancement for those wishing to progress.

long_description:
Yoga Nidra — Conscious Deep Sleep

Experience one of the most powerful methods of meditation: Yoga Nidra, the art of Conscious Deep Sleep. This ancient practice renews your energy, calms your mind, and restores balance on every level.
Yoga Nidra is one of the deepest forms of meditation. It gently guides your awareness through multiple layers of the mind, leading to a state of stillness, clarity, and profound insight.

Originally taught by wisdom teachers for exploring the deeper mind, Yoga Nidra helps uncover and purify the samskaras—the subtle impressions and past experiences that shape our desires, reactions, and actions (karma). Through entering the formless space of Conscious Deep Sleep, you can release these old imprints and experience true rest for both body and soul.

Whether you are new to meditation or have practiced for years, Yoga Nidra is simple and accessible. You’ll lie comfortably on your back, follow guided instructions, and drift into a deeply healing meditative state.

Benefits include:
• Deep relaxation and restoration for body and mind
• Reduced stress, anxiety, and emotional tension
• Improved sleep quality and nervous system balance
• Enhanced clarity, creativity, and inner awareness
• Release of old emotional patterns and subconscious blockages
• A greater sense of peace, contentment, and connection

All levels welcome.

What to bring:
Wear comfortable clothes and bring a light blanket (or something similar) to cover yourself during practice.

Mantra Yoga

Mantra Yoga is a meditative sound practice that activates healing, clarity, and awareness through the vibration of your own voice. Whether spoken, whispered, or chanted, each mantra becomes a tool for transformation.

In this class, we explore the pronunciation, meaning, and energy of sacred mantras. You may have heard them in Kundalini Yoga or other tradition and held back—this is your chance to deepen into their sound and fully experience their power.

Each session evolves organically, beginning with guided recitation, followed by call-and-response chanting, and devotional sound journeys. You’ll be supported by live harmonium, and from time to time, guest musicians who bring added depth to the experience.

Even if it’s your first time, all you need is an open heart. You’ll leave feeling lighter, more connected, and empowered by the vibration that lives within you.

Benefits include:
• Calms the mind and relieves anxiety
• Clears subconscious patterns and emotional blocks
• Strengthens vocal confidence and breath control
• Activates energy centers (chakras)
• Increases mental focus and inner peace
• Deepens meditation and devotional awareness
• Uplifts the spirit and fosters joy
• Awaken the power of your own voice.

A journey into healing sound, sacred words, and the vibration of consciousness. Let your voice lead the way. All levels welcome.

long_description:
In this session, we will explore what it actually takes to move AI agents from prototype to production-ready. We will cut through the AI hype and focus on the operational layer that teams need now: deployment, observability, governance, policy enforcement, and cloud-native agent management.

You will see a live demo of **WSO2 Agent Manager**, built on **OpenChoreo**, and learn how open source tooling can help teams manage agents at scale without reinventing the wheel.
This session is designed for builders who want to understand the future of AI deployment on AWS — not just how to create agents, but how to manage them responsibly in real-world environments.

## What This Session Will Cover

* How WSO2 Agent Manager and OpenChoreo support production-grade agent management
* How AI agents move from prototype to production
* Why governance matters before agent workflows scale
* How to deploy and manage agents in a cloud-native environment
* Why open source tools matter for teams building flexible AI infrastructure

## Key Takeaways

By the end of this session, you will walk away with:

* Open source tools and concepts you can start exploring immediately
* A clear framework for deploying and managing AI agents on AWS
* A practical understanding of agent governance, observability, and policy enforcement
* A live look at WSO2 Agent Manager + OpenChoreo
* Strategies for managing agents across environments

## Who Should Attend?

This event is for anyone who wants to grow in AI, AWS, cloud-native development, and modern technical delivery, including:

* Developers, Solutions engineers, Cloud engineers
* Product managers, AI strategists
* Startup builders, Technical founders

**Why You Need to Be Here (Uplevel Your Career!):** This isn't just another tech talk—it's a career accelerator! AI governance is currently the biggest bottleneck for enterprise AI adoption. By mastering how to safely govern and deploy agents to production, you instantly make yourself a high-value asset

long_description:
## Recess Cornhole League at Track 15

Join Recess for a 5-week singles cornhole league in the heart of downtown Providence at Track 15 — designed for adults looking to meet new people in a relaxed, low-pressure way. Whether you’re competitive or just there for the social atmosphere, this league is all about connection, conversation, and having fun.

### How It Works

**Weekly League Play**
Each week, participants will enjoy one hour of organized cornhole games with rotating teammates and opponents, making it easy to meet and interact with a variety of people throughout the night.
**Rotating Matches**
Players switch courts and partners approximately every 10–15 minutes, creating a fun, natural way to mingle without the awkwardness of traditional singles events.
**Post-Game Social Hour**
After league play wraps up, everyone is encouraged to stay, grab food or drinks, and continue socializing at Track 15. The best connections often happen after the games end.
**The Final Week Celebration**
Week 5 will feature a casual wrap-up social and mini party where participants can reconnect with people they met throughout the league and celebrate the season together.

### What to Expect

* Singles-only atmosphere
* Friendly and welcoming environment
* No cornhole experience necessary
* Come solo or with a friend
* Designed for genuine social connection, not pressure

### Location

Track 15 — Downtown Providence

### Time

Weekly evenings from 5:30 PM – 9:00 PM

long_description:
## **Yin Yoga Flow**

**Find Stillness. Release Tension. Restore Flow.'**

In a world that values constant movement, the **Yin Yoga Flow** is your invitation to slow down and turn inward. This practice targets the deeper "yin" tissues of the body - the fascia, ligaments, and joints rather than the superficial muscles, offering a profound sense of physical and mental release.
Unlike a traditional vinyasa class, this session focuses on long-held, passive floor poses, allowing the body to naturally open and the nervous system to shift into a state of deep rest.

### **The Practice**

* **Targeted Release:** Hold postures for 3–5 minutes to access connective tissues and improve joint mobility.
* **Mindful Presence:** Use the stillness to practice meditative awareness, observing sensations and thoughts without judgment.
* **Subtle Energy Flow:** Clear blockages in the body’s meridians to restore a sense of equilibrium and vitality.
* **Gentle Transitions:** Poses are linked with slow, intentional transitions to maintain a meditative state from start to finish.

### **Class Benefits**

* **Deep Flexibility:** Increases circulation and suppleness in the hips, pelvis, and lower spine.
* **Stress Reduction:** Activates the parasympathetic nervous system (rest and digest) to lower cortisol levels.
* **Mental Clarity:** Provides a quiet space to decompress and regulate your emotional engine.

**Best For:** All levels. Whether you are an athlete looking to recover or simply need a break from the digital noise, this class is your sanctuary.
**Leave feeling: Grounded, spacious, and deeply renewed.**

Donation Based: ($5-$25 Sliding Scale)

long_description:
✨ **An Evening of Reflection, Renewal and Awakening** ✨
Join us for a transformative evening of healing, connection, and self-discovery. Gathered in sacred space around the glow of the fire, we will journey together through meditations designed to ground, restore, and awaken the spirit to purpose and loving service.

🌿 **What to Expect**

* Gentle, guided meditations (two new practices each gathering)
* Heartfelt sharing in a safe, supportive circle
* Space for authentic expression, deep listening, and mutual growth
* Meaningful spiritual insights and uplifting discussion

This is a gathering for anyone seeking peace, clarity, or community. All are welcome—simply bring an open mind and a respectful heart.

🔥 **When & Where**

* We typically meet twice each month on the 2nd & 4th Thursdays. Come as often—or as little—as your spirit calls.
* Weather permitting, we gather outdoors in the tipi or by the large fire circle. If needed, we will move indoors.
*

💫 **For First-Time Visitors**

* No prior experience is needed.
* Please arrive **15 minutes early** to settle in.
* You are welcome to walk the grounds or explore our crystal shop before the circle begins.

📍 **Directions**

* Address: **15406 Riding Stable Rd.** (property is at the end of a ½ mile driveway into the woods).
* You will cross a small stream—drive slowly (under 10 MPH) to keep dust down.
* Please be mindful of our neighbors and do not stop to interact with horses along the way.
*

💖 **Energy Exchange**
To help keep this gathering accessible, we invite an offering of **$15–$25**. If you feel called to contribute in another way, please reach out in advance.

With love and gratitude, we welcome you into this circle of renewal.

Good conversation, good company, and a great beer to go with it! Let's share those tips and win in this challenging market!

long_description:
Sacred Dialogs is a guided inquiry circle exploring the spiritual philosophy of the Bhagavad Gītā as a foundational yoga text (Yoga Śāstra) and a practical guide for conscious living.
Rather than a lecture format, the session uses Community of Inquiry methods inspired by philosopher Matthew Lipman, creating a respectful, thoughtful space where participants explore questions together.

Topics may include:
• Purpose and meaning in yogic life
• The nature of the self and consciousness
• Action, intention, and inner freedom
• Applying yoga wisdom to modern daily life

Participants are encouraged to listen deeply, reflect honestly, and share at their own comfort level. No philosophical background is required—curiosity and openness are enough.
Each gathering concludes with a wholesome vegetarian dinner, allowing conversation to continue informally while fostering warmth, connection, and community.

Donations welcome.

description:
**The Art of Hands-On Adjustments & Assists**

Join us for an informative and experiential workshop designed for yoga teachers, teacher trainees, and dedicated students who wish to deepen their understanding of hands-on adjustments and assists. Rooted in the traditions of Astāṅga Yoga, skillful adjustments can help students experience greater alignment, stability, awareness, and ease within a posture while supporting the development of a safe and effective practice.

long_description:
**The Art of Hands-On Adjustments & Assists**

Join us for an informative and experiential workshop designed for yoga teachers, teacher trainees, and dedicated students who wish to deepen their understanding of hands-on adjustments and assists. Rooted in the traditions of Astāṅga Yoga, skillful adjustments can help students experience greater alignment, stability, awareness, and ease within a posture while supporting the development of a safe and effective practice.

This workshop will explore the principles behind effective assisting, including proper body mechanics, communication, observation skills, and the distinction between adjusting, assisting, and supporting. Participants will learn how to assess individual needs, apply appropriate levels of pressure and guidance, and offer adjustments that enhance rather than force a posture.
We will work through a wide range of postures from the standing, seated, and reclining sequences, as well as techniques for supporting students in relaxation and Śavāsana. Emphasis will be placed on maintaining the integrity of the pose, honoring individual differences, and cultivating confidence and sensitivity as an assistant.
Whether you are a teacher looking to refine your hands-on skills or a student curious about the role of adjustments in yoga practice, this workshop will provide practical tools, hands-on experience, and a deeper appreciation for the art of assisting others on the yoga path.

\*Yoga Alliance YACEP accredited hours available

long_description:
This life-changing, 4-day women’s Yosemite hiking adventure will give you jaw-dropping views of granite mountains, wide-open meadows, and ancient Sequoia trees. Maybe this trip is what your boss means when they demand leaving no stone unturned? Set that out of office and buy the hiking leggings with the deep pockets because your girl gang is WAITING FOR YOU.

With your new besties beside you and our professional guides showing you the good pee spots, we’ll explore the best Yosemite peaks and valleys in this crazy-beautiful playground. By day, we’ll clamber up towering domes and stroll through lush valleys. By nightfall, we’ll laugh until we can’t breathe and fall asleep smiling, snuggled up in our cozy cabins.

Enjoy a Google Earth view of Yosemite Valley from the top of Taft Point. Hike through a grove of forever-old Jeffrey Pines to summit Sentinel Dome. Feast on the panoramic majesty of Half Dome, Yosemite Falls, and Glacier Point. Seriously, this is your life right now, and you are HERE!

Hiking the famous Mist Trail will lead us through pristine wilderness to the deafening roar of Vernal and Nevada Falls. You’ll forget an entire household depends on you as you dash through the heart of Yosemite’s High Sierra meadows, taking a lunch break by a diamond-clear lake, surrounded by the towering granite peaks of the Cathedral Range.
We’ll cross wooden footbridges and babbling streams to stand inside a cathedral of trees, where sequoias stand like ancient sentinels. These living legends have names, personalities, and GOSSIP. You’ll meet Grizzly Giant, The Bachelor, Three Graces, and The Faithful Couple. (Or so they claim…)

Your only mission after the day’s Yosemite hike – eating, sleeping, and cackling with your new friends. No, you can’t help us with dishes. Yes, you can have seconds. Enjoy the feral highs of traveling with adult women who love and accept you just as you are.

long_description:
**Orlando Philosophy Field Day**
**Friday\, July 24\, 2026 \| 6:00 PM – 8:30 PM**
**Mead Botanical Garden \| Orlando\, FL**
**Free and open to the public**

Join us for **Orlando Philosophy Field Day**, an outdoor evening of big questions, fun games, and thoughtful conversation at Mead Botanical Garden.

This event is designed for anyone who enjoys thinking, discussing, questioning, or simply meeting curious people. No philosophy background is required. Whether you are brand new to philosophy or have been reading Plato, the Stoics, Nietzsche, critical theory, or modern ethics for years, this gathering is meant to be accessible, social, and engaging.
We will spend the evening exploring ideas through casual discussion, group activities, and conversation prompts. Expect a relaxed atmosphere where people can reflect, ask questions, share perspectives, and connect with others who enjoy meaningful dialogue.

**What to expect:**

* Big philosophical questions
* Fun games and activities
* Open conversations
* New perspectives
* Community and connection
* A welcoming space for beginners and experienced readers alike

This event is a collaboration between The Optimistic Nihilism Social Club, Orlando Stoics, Philosophy for Everyday Life, and Critical Theory Reading Group–Orlando.
Bring yourself, your curiosity, and a willingness to think, play, and discover.

**Philosophy is for everyone!**

**RSVP via:**

**Early Bird Discounts | More $ Later**

Hey night market fans!

Come soak in the glow of the string lights, the smell of sizzling street food, and the heavy bass of live beats right by the dance floor. Join me for an easy evening where we spend the first hour chatting one-on-one through the Gist IRL app, and then head out in small groups to grab some food, dance to Bhangra beats, and make some real connections along the way.

We'll kick things off with fast, friendly conversations. The app handles all the pairings, so you always know exactly who you're talking to and can just focus on breaking the ice with folks from all different backgrounds. Once we wrap up the rounds, you'll select the people you vibed with the most, and we'll group up to dive into the night market.

By the time you hit the dance floor, you've already got a fun crew to share the street food and live beats with. We'll be splitting into groups of 4-6, giving you a ready-made squad to grab some spicy skewers or a cold drink before migrating to the music. Whether these guys become your go-to night market and dancing squad or it's just a fantastic evening out under the stars, you're going to have a blast.

The Plan:

- 6:00PM: Check-In. Follow the link to set up your quick profile on your phone.
- 6:05PM - 7:25PM: One-on-One Rounds. The app pairs you up for some fun, focused chats. Find out who shares your love for vibrant cultural festivals, pulsing Punjabi beats, and delicious global street food.
- 7:25PM+: Group Up & Explore. Reconnect with the people you clicked with, form a tight crew of 4-6, grab some food from the trucks, snag a drink from the outdoor bars, and head over to the dance floor together.

San Francisco’s [beloved celebration](https://www.instagram.com/p/DZUIqzoyCQ8/) returns with a major new milestone: for the first time ever, Bhangra & Beats will take place at Yerba Buena Gardens, one of downtown San Francisco’s most iconic arts and cultural destinations.

This FREE event will transform Yerba Buena Gardens, Jessie Square, and Yerba Buena Lane into an open-air festival of music, dance, food, and community. [Non Stop Bhangra ](https://www.instagram.com/nonstopbhangra/)collective will once again lead the experience with its signature mix of interactive dance lessons, beautiful performances, live dhol drumming, DJs, and an open dance floor, all flowing into a lively marketplace with food vendors, local makers, community activations, restaurant and bar specials, and family-friendly activities.

You will go on about 10 dates with someone of the opposite sex, each date will be 7 minutes long/short. We will provide you with materials to tell us who you liked. Women 30 - 45, Men 30 - 45

* We are promoting this event on various dating sites, don't just go by the number of people who have RSVP'd on this Meetup group. This event is almost sold out.

Thank you all for your patience while I was MIA for a little while. It’s great to be back, and I’m excited for our next Dining experience!

We’ll be visiting Pop Thai, a restaurant I’ve found that has wonderful reviews. One of my absolute favorite Thai dishes is Khao Soi, a Northern Thai curry noodle soup that’s difficult to find in the U.S. Another favorite is Larb, a minced meat salad that’s a staple in Thailand.

They can comfortably accommodate us, and I’m looking forward to seeing how their authentic Thai dishes compare to the incredible food I’ve enjoyed during my trips to Thailand.

Whether you’re already a fan of Thai cuisine or trying it for the first time, I hope you’ll join us for a night of great food, great conversation, and another fun cultural dining experience.

Looking forward to seeing everyone again!

long_description:
Join us for an uplifting evening of devotion and community at our Bhakti Kirtan, guided by the inspiring Subala Das! Immerse yourself in the soulful vibrations of mantra chanting, led by Subal and passionate kirtaniyas who bring the sacred sounds to life. Kirtan is a beautiful practice of call-and-response singing that opens the heart, uplifts the spirit, and connects us with the divine through the practice of bhakti.

Bhakti, a Sanskrit word meaning “devotion” or “love,” is the spiritual path of connecting with the divine through heartfelt surrender and loving service. It emphasizes cultivating a deep, personal relationship with the divine, often expressed through music, prayer, and acts of kindness. Bhakti transcends religious boundaries, welcoming everyone into its embrace of universal love.

This event is open to everyone, whether you’re new to kirtan or a seasoned practitioner. Come as you are and leave feeling nourished—body, mind, and soul. Bring your friends and family, and experience the joy of chanting and sharing a meal together in a warm and welcoming atmosphere!

**Surya Kriya** is a potent yoga of tremendous antiquity, designed as a holistic process for health, wellness, and complete inner well-being. **“*Surya*”** means **“sun,”** and **“*kriya*”** means **“inner energy process.”** Surya Kriya activates the solar plexus to raise the *samat prana*, or solar heat, in the system. It also balances a person’s left and right energy channels, leading to stability of the body and stillness of the mind. This strong foundation becomes the basis to explore higher dimensions of life.

Traditionally available only to select groups of yogis, Surya Kriya is being offered by Sadhguru as a comprehensive spiritual practice that is ideal for the hectic pace of today’s world.
This is a hatha yoga program (physical postures) which will be taught step-by-step and guided by a teacher trained in India by Sadhguru. Once you have completed the program, you can practice on your own at home. Surya Kriya does not require previous experience with yoga.

**Benefits:**

* Develops mental clarity and focus
* Remedies weak constitutions
* Boosts vigor and vitality
* Balances hormonal levels in the body
* Prepares one for deeper states of meditation

long_description:
Join us on July 25 at Sarva in Back Bay as we discuss *The Loneliness of Sonia & Sunny* by Kiran Desai.

Nearly twenty years after winning the Booker Prize for *The Inheritance of Loss*, Kiran Desai returns with an ambitious novel that spans continents, generations, and cultures. At its heart is the story of Sonia and Sunny, two young Indians whose lives intersect between India and the United States as they search for love, purpose, and a sense of belonging in an increasingly globalized world. What begins as a chance encounter unfolds into a sweeping exploration of family, identity, migration, class, and the ties that connect us across time and distance.
Desai's novel is both an intimate love story and an expansive family saga, filled with vivid characters, sharp observations, and reflections on what it means to build a life between cultures. Through Sonia and Sunny's journeys, the novel examines loneliness not simply as isolation, but as a universal human experience shaped by history, family expectations, and the search for connection.

As always, our discussion will be relaxed, welcoming, and accompanied by excellent food. Whether you read every page, are still making your way through this doorstopper of a novel, or are simply curious about contemporary South Asian literature, we'd love to have you join us.
📖 Book: *The Loneliness of Sonia & Sunny* by Kiran Desai
📍 Location: Sarva, Back Bay
📅 Date: July 25
Come for the fiction, stay for the food and conversation.

long_description:
**Women's Circle on the Lake**

Gather in the company of other women in a mindfulness circle on Lake Michigan. Get in touch with your intuition and power during a guided meditation, breathwork, gentle stretching, and yoga. Leave firmly rooted, inspired, and grounded to start the week ahead!

Please note: this is a paid women's circle; the ticket cost is $10. Pay by Venmo or cash at the start of the circle.

Hosted by Yulia Denisyuk, a veteran [travel journalist](https://www.yulia-denisyuk.com/), host of the [Going Places platform](https://goingplacesmedia.com/), and teacher who's traveled to over 100 countries in search of wisdom. During a women's circle at the Temple of Moon in Peru, Yulia felt the call to continue these gatherings back home – and she followed the call.

This is not a yoga session. This is a gathering for women to practice gentle meditation, mindfulness, stretching, and a few yoga poses meant to activate our intuition and inner wisdom.

Practical info:
\- The session will last about 1 hour\, with about 10 minutes before and after to prep and wind down\. Total time: \~ 1 hour and 10 minutes
\- Bring your own yoga mat or a blanket to sit on\.
\- The session will be on the shore of Lake Michigan in Lakeview\. We'll gather in a shaded\, tree\-lined part of the shore\.

long_description:

Every day, the weather feels more and more like summer! Trees are leafing and flowers are blooming! Time to think about summer and heading into the Sandias! So, we're thinking about plans for the Annual Sierra Club Picnic! Sierra Club members and friends are invited to join us for a potluck of yummy offerings, plus panoramic views, bird watching, fresh air and sunshine!

Here are the details:
**When:** July 25, 2026, 10 am to 2 pm
**Where:** *Capulin Springs Picnic Area in the Cibola National Forest*. For details, visit [http:www.rec.gov ](http://http:www.rec.gov)
Some highlights - This picnic site is surrounded by heavily wooded land that affords shade to escape the heat of the day. The spring at Capulin Spring runs year-round and is a much visited spot by birders, especially in the dry season because thirsty birds flock to this area for a nice, cool drink of water. Bring a potluck offering to share.

*If your last name starts with A-H, bring a main entree; last name starts with I-S, appetizers and salads; last name starts with T-Z, dessert. Drinks, chips, plates, utensils and napkins will be provided by the Central Group.*

Bring a friend!
