**About the event:**
In restorative yoga, deep relaxation, supported postures, gentle breathing, and meditation work together to ease stress. The focus is on opening and relaxation, not strength or flexibility. This class will consist of only a handful of postures that are held for between 5-10 minutes, with the support of props like blocks, bolsters, and blankets to ease your body and nervous system into a deeper state of relaxation.

**What to bring?**
Please wear comfortable, warm clothes (i.e. sweat pants, sweatshirts, warm socks) and bring a water bottle with you. Yoga mats and all props will be provided, but feel free to bring your own, if you wish.

Please arrive on time. The door will be locked while class is in session to avoid disruptions.

long_description:
Let's have another book club on the beach! We will meet in Lewes June!

For anyone who hasn't joined in Lewes, we will meet on the corner of the large parking lot. We walk together to go get ice cream, go back and grab our chairs/blankets to sit on, and get settled on the beach after that.

**Book:**
The Unhoneymooners by Christina Lauren

**About:**
Olive is always unlucky: in her career, in love, in…well, everything. Her identical twin sister Ami, on the other hand, is probably the luckiest person in the world. Her meet-cute with her fiancé is something out of a romantic comedy (gag) and she’s managed to finance her entire wedding by winning a series of Internet contests (double gag). Worst of all, she’s forcing Olive to spend the day with her sworn enemy, Ethan, who just happens to be the best man. Olive braces herself to get through 24 hours of wedding hell before she can return to her comfortable, unlucky life. But when the entire wedding party gets food poisoning from eating bad shellfish, the only people who aren’t affected are Olive and Ethan. And now there’s an all-expenses-paid honeymoon in Hawaii up for grabs. Putting their mutual hatred aside for the sake of a free vacation, Olive and Ethan head for paradise, determined to avoid each other at all costs. But when Olive runs into her future boss, the little white lie she tells him is suddenly at risk to become a whole lot bigger. She and Ethan now have to pretend to be loving newlyweds, and her luck seems worse than ever. But the weird thing is that she doesn’t mind playing pretend. In fact, she feels kind of... lucky.

No doubt AI is changing a lot about our economy, techno
long_description:
Join us this month for a fascinating and timely fireside chat with a power-packed panel of startup community builders, moderated by COED's Jonathan Chambers on AI and Community, "Human Advantage: Why Community Still Wins in the Age of AI", featuring Julie Pierre, Community & Ecosystem Development at Tech Square; Nisha Kavalam, Vice President of Operations & Marketing of Atlanta Tech Week; Ania Lackey, Executive Director of FinTech Atlanta.

No doubt AI is changing a lot about our economy, technology, culture, and how we do business. Even how we interact and relate to each other in community. But, has it replaced and redefined what it means to be a community and build a thriving community within that AI-driven economy? Hear from some of Atlanta's top innovation leaders and startup community builders at the cusp of technology, AI, and startups and how they continue to keep the human element strong and present in building a thriving, connected, and innovative community.

Whether you're in tech, startups, community, and any level of AI use, you'll leave with fresh reminders of the power of the human advantage of community in the age of AI.

long_description:
**🌐 CONNECTED BY WIRE, APART BY HEART**
We have more ways to connect than any generation in history—yet loneliness has become one of the defining challenges of our time.
Join a world-traveling swami for an inspiring evening exploring the ancient yoga wisdom that helps us cultivate genuine connection in an age of deep disconnection.
We swipe, scroll, and double-tap through thousands of lives every day, yet many of us feel unseen, unheard, and alone.
**📊 The numbers tell the story:**
• Nearly half of young adults report experiencing loneliness
• Many of us check our phones 100+ times a day, mistaking stimulation for connection
• More people than ever report having few—or no—close friends they can rely on
✨ **Swami on Overcoming Loneliness** is not a self-help seminar or a lecture. It is an invitation to step away from the noise and explore a deeper understanding of connection, belonging, and fulfillment.
Drawing from timeless yoga philosophy, the swami will share practical insights into why we feel disconnected, how the mind creates separation, and what we can do to experience authentic relationships—with others and ourselves.
**🧘 The Evening Includes:**
• Insightful talk on overcoming loneliness and cultivating meaningful connection
• Guided meditation for inner stillness
• Restorative sound bath for deep relaxation
• Nourishing vegan dinner shared in community
🌿 For one evening, put down the phone, step into the room, and experience a different kind of connection.
You may leave with more than inspiration—you may leave with a new way of relating to yourself and the world around you.

long_description:
Breathe deeply, touch the earth, look up at the sky.

This summer and through September, we are taking our practice out of the studio and into the fresh air. Join us for outdoor sessions designed to help you ground your energy, build strength, and connect with the community in our beautiful local green spaces. All levels are welcome, from complete beginners to experienced practitioners.

Practicing outdoors is wonderful, but it does require a tiny bit of extra preparation. Here is what you should bring to get the most out of your session:

* A Yoga Mat or Large Towel
* Water
* Optional: yoga blocks and strap
* Arrive a few minutes early to find your spot and settle in.

Please also register in advance with the Town of Windsor [here](https://secure.rec1.com/CT/town-windsor/catalog/index/e56fcd7931ad028f636d7158daa218ed?filter=c2VhcmNoPUZyYW5r).

Yoga is a way to get to know our bodies better, calm our ever-thinking minds and enjoy some inner peace. Treat yourself to 90 minutes self-care. Leave class refreshed and rejuvenated! Feel free to leave questions in the comments section or message me on meetup.

Class includes breath-work, postures, correct alignment, relaxation, meditation, and yogic wisdom. Modifications to postures are suggested to accommodate individual needs.

Our bodies are unique so beginners are encouraged to take their time and adapt slowly to the postures, resting as they deem appropriate for their bodies. Props such as chairs, blocks, straps, bolsters and blankets are available in studio to assist you.

Yoga is a practice that cultivates joy, concentration, mindfulness, body awareness, flexibility, health and serenity. Simply put, yoga is fun. It is not a sequence of masochistic exercises!

This does not mean we practice yoga haphazardly. Quite the contrary. We bring body, breath, mental focus and magnanimous spirit to every asana (posture.) We are fully present . . . but without strain, tension, self-judgment or perfectionism.

My name is Frank .

long_description:
Bring your yoga mat, blanket, and any other comfort items as you will be laying down for this deeply healing session.
Transformational Breathwork is a powerful ACTIVE breathing meditation for self-healing. This practice appeals especially to people who enjoy yoga, as it addresses the mind, body, and spirit of the individual.
You will be learning a 2 stage 'pranayama yoga' breath, which is the active portion of the practice, and sometimes called the 'work' part of breathwork. The active breathing segment is followed by an integration, or rest period. This is all done to specific music while lying down on a yoga mat. Bolsters, blankets are recommended, eye masks are provided.

This is a specific, rhythmic breathing pattern that can help clear out emotions and stuck energy. It literally quiets the mind so that the heart can open and heal. A modality that must be experienced to appreciate.

This is a RWJ Community Event.

$15 per person
Call 609-584-5900 to register.

long_description:
Mantra Yoga

Mantra Yoga is a meditative sound practice that activates healing, clarity, and awareness through the vibration of your own voice. Whether spoken, whispered, or chanted, each mantra becomes a tool for transformation.

In this class, we explore the pronunciation, meaning, and energy of sacred mantras. You may have heard them in Kundalini Yoga or other tradition and held back—this is your chance to deepen into their sound and fully experience their power.

Each session evolves organically, beginning with guided recitation, followed by call-and-response chanting, and devotional sound journeys. You’ll be supported by live harmonium, and from time to time, guest musicians who bring added depth to the experience.

Even if it’s your first time, all you need is an open heart. You’ll leave feeling lighter, more connected, and empowered by the vibration that lives within you.

Benefits include:
• Calms the mind and relieves anxiety
• Clears subconscious patterns and emotional blocks
• Strengthens vocal confidence and breath control
• Activates energy centers (chakras)
• Increases mental focus and inner peace
• Deepens meditation and devotional awareness
• Uplifts the spirit and fosters joy
• Awaken the power of your own voice.

A journey into healing sound, sacred words, and the vibration of consciousness. Let your voice lead the way. All levels welcome.

What to bring:
Wear comfortable clothes (white cotton is suggested for its uplifting energy, but not required.)

Join Service Design DC and our friends at MediaBarn for our annual Summer Social, a relaxed evening dedicated to connection, conversation, and community.

**This is your chance to:**

* Meet fellow service design practitioners, students, and enthusiasts from across the DMV.

**Many thanks to our host and sponsor, MediaBarn!**

long_description:
Here's the agenda for this Meetup:

Please note we will start promptly at 12:00 pm. Please be a few minutes early so you will have time to order some lunch. Also, give yourself a few minutes to catch up with other members. This will ensure that we can start on time and then we will be able to leave on time.
We do ask that as we get back to in-person networking, you WILL NEED

• We'll do a brief introduction of ABNG and also quickly go over our rules (don't worry, there's only three and a half!). Then, we'll get right to the meeting.

• Hold on to your business cards for now. We will start the meeting by going around the room with our introductions. Notice we didn't say 30-second commercial or elevator pitch. There's a fantastic TED talk ([https://youtu.be/u4ZoJKF_VuA](https://youtu.be/u4ZoJKF_VuA)) from Simon Sinek that might blow you away.

• After introductions, we'll do our shoutouts and share our member events. If you had a great 1:1 with someone or have some other awesome thing to share, we have the space for that! If you have a workshop, class, meeting or event coming up, this is a great time to inform the group. We will also discuss specific needs you may have. Do you need a resource of some kind? Chances are someone in our group can point you in the right direction.

• If time allows, we will engage in our Mastermind discussion. If you feel like you have something in your business that is holding you back, this is time and the place to tackle it. If you have something that you need help with, make sure to let the host know before the meeting starts so that we can make time for it during our meeting. The power of the group is immense!

• We'll close out our meeting by passing around business cards and ensuring you have time to set up your 1:1's before adjourning at 1:00 p.m.
We look forward to seeing you at our next meeting!

long_description:
Whether you're preparing to meet investors, talk to customers, launch your product, or simply want feedback from fellow founders, this meetup is for you.

**Note:** We’re capping this meetup at 30 people. Only 10 spots are available to RSVP on Meetup - feel free to join the waitlist and I’ll approve additional attendees until we reach capacity.

Bring your startup, business idea, MVP, prototype, or side project and give a short pitch. If you have a product, prototype, landing page, or mockup, we encourage you to give a brief demo as well. Demos are encouraged but not required - if you don't have something to show yet, you're still welcome to pitch and receive valuable feedback.

After each pitch (and demo, if applicable), attendees will have the opportunity to ask questions and provide constructive feedback on your messaging, product, and overall approach. Whether you have an established business, an early MVP, or are still validating your idea, you'll gain valuable insights to help you move forward.

After everyone has had a chance to pitch, we'll transition into a casual networking and co-working session. Stick around to continue conversations, exchange ideas, make new connections, or spend some time working alongside other founders.

Whether you're pitching for the first time or the fiftieth - or simply attending to learn - come ready to support fellow entrepreneurs, share your perspective, and connect with other builders in the DC area.

long_description:
Join SUP Frederick for our annual 32-mile downriver paddle adventure on the Potomac River from Brunswick, MD to Violette’s Lock!

📆 August 1–2, 2026

Whether this is your first LONG distance paddle or you’re one of our returning 32-Miler alumni… you’ll love the challenge!

This is NOT a race; it’s a laid-back, long-distance journey down the Potomac River. We take breaks, move together, enjoy the scenery, and settle into the rhythm of the river one mile at a time. 🌊

This event is known for great people, beautiful scenery, snack breaks, stories, and a whole lot of river miles.

Paddle boards, kayaks, canoes, and adventure seekers welcome.

📍 ROUTE
Brunswick Boat Ramp → Violette’s Lock = 32 miles

🕘 DAY ONE
Meet: 8:30 AM
Launch: 9:00 AM sharp
📍 Brunswick Boat Ramp(near the MARC train station). We’ll paddle approximately 16 miles downstream on day one before camping overnight at 🏕️ Marble Quarry Hiker-Biker Campsite (one of the many first-come, first-serve campsites with fire pit + restroom access)

☕ DAY TWO
We break camp in the morning and paddle downstream to White’s Ferry (see menu here: https://www.whitesferrygrill.com) for breakfast / coffee / regroup / resupply before the final stretch to Violette’s Lock

🚣 This paddle is definitely for everybody, with so many options. You can:

• Paddle the full 32 miles with us over two days
• Paddle day one only (launch with us from Brunswick at 9:00 AM and exit at any of the boat ramps along the route).
• Join for day two only near White’s Ferry (meet us for coffee/breakfast before launching downstream with the group).
• Camp with us overnight and spend the weekend hiking or biking the C&O Canal Towpath.
• Meet up with the group anywhere along the route at one of the many launch/takeout points, just message me and I’ll give you ETA to next ramp/meeting point (reach out to me in advance).

description:

long_description:
Just east of Las Vegas lies one of Southern Nevada's most colorful and overlooked landscapes. While Lava Butte is interesting from the ground, its true beauty reveals itself from above in the morning light, where layers of red, yellow, orange, and tan hills create abstract patterns that seem more at home in a painting than the Mojave Desert.

This event is specifically designed for drone photographers looking to capture a perspective that simply can't be appreciated from ground level. We'll explore the area at a relaxed pace, searching for the best aerial compositions, colorful ridgelines, winding washes, and the unique textures that make Lava Butte such a hidden gem. Whether you're an experienced pilot or just looking to gain more flight time in a spectacular location, this is a great opportunity to photograph one of the most drone-friendly landscapes near Las Vegas.

**MEETUP INFO:**
We will meet at 6:30am at Sunrise Trailhead. This is just a 30 minute drive from Las Vegas (on the east side of the city by Wetlands Park). Please plan accordingly to arrive on time.

From there, we will drive about 20 minutes down Lava Butte Road on a gravel road that is not recommended for low clearance vehicles. However, it does not require 4WD / AWD. Carpooling is available (I personally would have room for 3 passengers).

**MEETUP FEES:**
There are no fees for this event.

**PHYSICAL ACTIVITY:**
There is minimal walking required, as we will drive into Lava Butte and be able to fly right from our vehicles. Those wishing to explore additional viewpoints may choose to walk short distances over uneven desert terrain.

**ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:**
Please ensure your drone is charged, updated, and ready to fly prior to arrival.

If your plans change and you are unable to attend, please be courteous and cancel your RSVP so that someone else can attend.

long_description:
After his home is destroyed and his parents are killed in the Iran-Iraq war, Bashu, a small, dark-skinned boy from the Arabic-speaking Persian Gulf region of Iran, escapes on a truck to the northern part of the country, bordering the Caspian Sea. There he is taken in by Na’i, a peasant woman raising her own two children alone because her husband, who lost an arm in the war, is elsewhere in the country seeking employment. Since Na’i speaks only Gilaki, a local tongue, she and Bashu have no language in common. But over time they form a strong bond.

[Click here to watch a short scene from the film](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JSDcbZMVo58)

Stop by Friday for an evening of drumming, singing, and meditation!

Bring your own drum or use one of ours - no experience needed!

There will be loose guidance of a rhythmic drumming session, weaving in contemporary kirtan to inspire singing and dancing.

This is a donation-based gathering-pay what you can, with a suggested contribution of $15.

**🌿 About The Karma House**
The Karma House isn’t your average bar — we’re an alcohol-free kava bar and community hub in Lakewood, CO. Our space was created to bring people together through music, art, wellness, and connection. From live shows to poetry nights to wellness workshops, everything we do centers around community and creating a safe, welcoming atmosphere for all.
**🥥 What is a Kava Bar?**
Kava bars are unique gathering places where people come to connect and unwind without alcohol. Instead of cocktails, we serve traditional Polynesian kava — a calming root tea that has been used for centuries in the South Pacific for relaxation, stress relief, and social connection.
**🍵 What is Kava?**
Kava is made from the root of the Piper methysticum plant. It has gentle, grounding effects that can help calm the body and quiet the mind, making it perfect for relaxing, connecting, and enjoying good company. At The Karma House, we prepare our shells of kava with care and community in mind — it’s more than a drink, it’s a ritual of connection.

long_description:
Step away from the noise and settle into an afternoon of reflection, music, and meaningful conversation.

Sounds of Wisdom is a unique contemplative experience that blends the soothing sounds of the handpan with nature-inspired soundscapes, thought-provoking monologues, guided meditations, and selected excerpts from Jaxon Phoenix’s book Only Us, designed to encourage presence, curiosity, and inner peace.

As the music unfolds, you’ll be invited to relax with a warm cup of tea or coffee, allowing the gentle rhythms of the handpan and the reflections woven throughout the experience to create space for stillness, insight, and self-discovery.

This is not a lecture, and it is not a concert. It is a gathering for those who long to slow down, think deeply, and reconnect with themselves and the world around them.

Whether you’re seeking inspiration, clarity, or simply a peaceful place to breathe, Sounds of Wisdom offers an opportunity to pause and listen—not only to the music, but to the wisdom that often emerges in moments of quiet contemplation.

Stay afterward for tea, conversation, and signed copies of Only Us, available for purchase following the event.

Come comfortable. Bring an open mind. Leave feeling grounded, refreshed, and inspired.

long_description:
**AIMUG Monthly Mixer & Showcase**
**Austin LangChain + AI Middleware Users Group**
**Time:** 6:00 PM – 8:30 PM
**Venue:** ACC – RGC 3000, 1218 West Avenue, Austin, TX
**After-Party:** The Tavern, 922 W 12th St, Austin, TX

***

**Quick Summary**
Join us for the monthly AIMUG Mixer & Showcase — an evening of practical demos, short deep-dives, and relaxed community networking.
We focus on **agentic software development**: multi-agent architectures, middleware patterns, **LangChain + LangGraph** workflows, **DeepAgents**, and real-world a**pplication building**.
Many presenters are power users of **Claude Code**, and we frequently explore how developers use it in their agent workflows.

***

**Run of Show (Template / Reusable)**
**6:00 – 6:20 PM — Networking & Welcome**
Grab a drink, meet other AI practitioners, settle in.
**6:20 – 6:30 PM — Introductions & Kickoff (10 min)**
Brief community intros + overview of the agenda.
**6:30 – 7:40 PM — Thunderstorm Talks (15 min each)**

* **Thunderstorm Talk Slot 1 (15 min)**
* **Thunderstorm Talk Slot 2 (15 min)**
* **Thunderstorm Talk Slot 3 (15 min)**
* **Thunderstorm Talk Slot 4 (15 min)**

**7:40 – 8:00 PM — Buffer & Open Q&A**
Follow up with speakers, demo projects, or run long if needed.
*Target wrap-up: \~7:45–8:00 PM; venue clears by 8:30 PM.*
**8:00 – 8:30 PM — Walk to After-Party**
Casual mixer continues at **The Tavern**.

***

**About AIMUG**
AIMUG is built on the philosophy of **Learning in the Open**.
We explore the entire agentic stack — LangChain, LangGraph, LangSmith, DeepAgents, Claude Code, Claude Skills/Subagents, and the broader AI middleware ecosystem.
Expect demos, patterns, pitfalls, and community-built insights from developers shipping real agent-powered applications.
We’re graciously hosted by the Center for Government & Civic Service at ACC’s Rio Grande Campus.

***

long_description:
Sacred Dialogs is a guided inquiry circle exploring the spiritual philosophy of the Bhagavad Gītā as a foundational yoga text (Yoga Śāstra) and a practical guide for conscious living.
Rather than a lecture format, the session uses Community of Inquiry methods inspired by philosopher Matthew Lipman, creating a respectful, thoughtful space where participants explore questions together.

Topics may include:
• Purpose and meaning in yogic life
• The nature of the self and consciousness
• Action, intention, and inner freedom
• Applying yoga wisdom to modern daily life

Participants are encouraged to listen deeply, reflect honestly, and share at their own comfort level. No philosophical background is required—curiosity and openness are enough.
Each gathering concludes with a wholesome vegetarian dinner, allowing conversation to continue informally while fostering warmth, connection, and community.

long_description:
**This event is posted on behalf of the Westerly Land Trust. Registration is required outside of Meetup. [Please register here.](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/paddle-yoga-float-flow-registration-1993347180075)**

Certified yoga teacher, Janice Fifer, will guide us through Sun Salutations with a focus on hip and shoulder openers to prepare for a paddle up the Pawcatuck River. We will stop along the way for a short meditation and ride the river’s gentle current back to the put-in point. The day will end with relaxation and a closing circle. This is a moderate paddle for kayakers with some experience, with the emphasis on relaxing and enjoying nature.

**What to bring:** BYO Kayak, Paddle board, canoe etc, Paddle, Life Jacket, Yoga Mat, Large Towel (to put under your yoga mat), Water, Bug Repellent. Be aware that your shoes will get wet and muddy.

**Please note:** Rhode Island State Regulations require that everyone, regardless of age, MUST wear a US Coast Guard approved life jacket, fastened in the manner the manufacturer intended.

**Parking:** Parking is available at Flora Whitely Preserve at [197 Potter Hill Rd](https://www.google.com/maps/place/197+Potter+Hill+Rd,+Westerly,+RI+02891/@41.4137429,-71.7974699,21z/data=!4m5!3m4!1s0x89e5dd6e2199da8f:0xd825c68fe1fa552!8m2!3d41.4136666!4d-71.797423?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDYyOS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D "https://www.google.com/maps/place/197+Potter+Hill+Rd,+Westerly,+RI+02891/@41.4137429,-71.7974699,21z/data=!4m5!3m4!1s0x89e5dd6e2199da8f:0xd825c68fe1fa552!8m2!3d41.4136666!4d-71.797423?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDYyOS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D"). We will put in for our paddle there as well.
This event is **FREE** for members, and $10 per person for not-yet members. Not a member and would like to be? [CLICK HERE](https://westerlylandtrust.org/support-our-work/make-a-gift/ "https://westerlylandtrust.org/support-our-work/make-a-gift/")!
Registration required, spots are limited.

long_description:
Sacred Dialogs is a guided inquiry circle exploring the spiritual philosophy of the Bhagavad Gītā as a foundational yoga text (Yoga Śāstra) and a practical guide for conscious living.
Rather than a lecture format, the session uses Community of Inquiry methods inspired by philosopher Matthew Lipman, creating a respectful, thoughtful space where participants explore questions together.

Topics may include:
• Purpose and meaning in yogic life
• The nature of the self and consciousness
• Action, intention, and inner freedom
• Applying yoga wisdom to modern daily life

Participants are encouraged to listen deeply, reflect honestly, and share at their own comfort level. No philosophical background is required—curiosity and openness are enough. Each gathering concludes with a wholesome vegetarian dinner, allowing conversation to continue informally while fostering warmth, connection, and community. Donations welcome.

long_description:
**A 90-minute vinyasa flow journey in the fresh air of the Wasatch mountains**

Drop into meditation, move through a full vinyasa flow, and then drape a cool lavender towel over your eyes for an extended savasana.

**Saturday, August 22nd 9:30-11:00 am @ Brighton Ski Resort**

You’ll already be up the canyon, so bring a friend and a picnic for a hike! It’s a ready-made self-care day ❤️

**Reserve a spot with a donation (recommended: $15-25)**
Venmo @emcapito with the “Brighton August” and your email for updates, and you are absolutely welcome to just show up!

**This is a community offering, so if the budget is tight or it’s your first time and you’d prefer to decide if you’d like to donate after, everyone is invited!**

* Suitable for all levels.
* Bring your own mat, water and sunscreen/sunglasses.
* Dress in layers – Utah weather is unpredictable!
* I also recommend socks just in case your mat gets hot in the sunshine.
* Ages 12 and up. Minors must have a parent/guardian present.

**Plan travel time so that you have at least 10 minutes to settle in.** The canyon always takes a little longer than expected. Give yourself a cushion and enjoy the beautiful drive.

**DIRECTIONS:**
Map: https://goo.gl/maps/f3ffkpHRvF2GtVce7
Brighton is at the top of Big Cottonwood Canyon. We will meet on the patio on the back of the Milly Chalet, which is the first building on your right as you turn into the large Brighton parking lot. It’s one level and cream colored next to a lift.

**Questions? Lost?** Text 801-898-0842

**Many thanks to Brighton Resort** **for hosting us over the years!**

Programs are on Thursday and Friday evenings for 3 1/4 hours and continue all day on Saturday and Sunday.
Vegetarian lunch is provided on Saturday; Vegetarian breakfast & lunch on Sunday.

Thursday, August 27th , 6:00 PM - 9:15 PM

- Admission: Free and open to all

long_description:
Restorative aerial yoga class is a deeply relaxing practice combining the gentle support of an aerial silk hammock with restorative yoga.
Cloud 9 Restorative Aerial Yoga
Tickets: $26.00
This restorative aerial yoga class is a deeply relaxing practice that combines the gentle support of an aerial silk hammock with restorative yoga postures to promote healing, relaxation, and balance.
In this class, you'll experience the sensation of being weightless as the hammock supports your body, allowing you to release tension, stretch more deeply, and improve flexibility without strain.
The poses are held for longer periods, encouraging mindfulness, soothing the nervous system, and promoting deep rest.
Whether you're new to aerial yoga or an experienced yogi, this class will help you find balance, ease, and a renewed sense of calm.
Join us on the 1st and 3rd Thursdays each month from 7:00 to 8:30 PM for a transformative experience that leaves you feeling refreshed and revitalized.

title: Paryushan & Das Lakshana — Jain Center of Northern California
description: Ten-day Jain holy period of Paryushan and Das Lakshana with fasting, meditation, and forgiveness rituals.
long_description: Paryushan and Das Lakshana is the most important annual Jain observance — ten days of fasting, meditation, scripture reading, and self-reflection. The Jain Center of Northern California hosts daily programs including pratikraman, lectures, and the Samvatsari festival of forgiveness. The final day features the Kshamapana ceremony where Jains ask forgiveness from all living beings.
venue_info: 722 S Main St, Milpitas, CA 95035. Daily programs. Parking on-site. Vegetarian food only.

long_description: Krishna Janmashtami is celebrated with an evening-to-midnight program at the Shiva Vishnu Temple. The festivities include special abhishekam of Lord Krishna, devotional bhajans, cultural performances, and the grand midnight aarti marking the exact time of Krishna's birth. The temple is beautifully decorated with flowers and lights for this beloved festival.
venue_info: 1232 Arrowhead Ave, Livermore. Special extended hours for Janmashtami (until past midnight). Expect large crowds — arrive early for parking. Prasadam served throughout.

title: Bank of America Chicago Marathon 2026
description: One of the six World Marathon Majors. A flat, fast course through Chicago's diverse neighborhoods with 53,000 runners and 1.7 million spectators.
long_description: The Bank of America Chicago Marathon is one of the six World Marathon Majors and the 48th edition of this iconic race. Over 53,000 runners from 130+ countries run a flat, fast course through 29 Chicago neighborhoods. The 2026 race continues the tradition of record-breaking performances on one of the fastest courses in the world. With 1.7 million spectators lining the streets, the energy is electric from start to finish.
venue_info: Start and finish in Grant Park, downtown Chicago. The course is famously flat with minimal elevation change. CTA trains (Red, Blue, Green lines) serve Grant Park. The Abbott Health & Fitness Expo takes place at McCormick Place the days before. 6-hour 30-minute time limit.

Live music, traditional dance, and nightly Devi pujas draw hundreds of families from across metro Atlanta. Traditional attire — colorful chaniya choli and kediya — fills the dance floor nightly.

description: Nine nights of Navratri garba and dandiya at the Boston area's Sri Lakshmi Temple in Ashland.
long_description: Sri Lakshmi Temple hosts the Boston area's premier Navratri celebration with nine nights of garba and dandiya. Live music, traditional dance, and devotional programs draw hundreds of families from across Massachusetts and neighboring states. One of New England's largest Hindu festival celebrations.

long_description: Bharatiya Temple hosts the Detroit area's most popular Navratri celebration with nine nights of energetic garba and dandiya. Each evening features live music, traditional dance, and devotional programs. The temple's spacious hall accommodates hundreds of dancers. Traditional attire — chaniya choli for women, kurta for men — is the norm.
venue_info: 6850 Adams Rd, Troy, MI 48098. Large parking lot. Refreshments and festival food available. Air-conditioned hall.

title: Navratri & Dussehra — BAPS Mandir, Chicago
description: Navratri celebrations at Chicago's stunning BAPS marble mandir with garba, dandiya, and devotional programs.
long_description: The BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Bartlett hosts Chicago's most spectacular Navratri celebration. Nine evenings of garba and dandiya in the temple's magnificent marble halls create an unforgettable atmosphere. The mandir — the largest Hindu temple in Illinois — features hand-carved Italian marble and Turkish limestone architecture that glows beautifully during the festival.
venue_info: 1851 Jens Jensen Blvd, Bartlett, IL 60103. Free parking. Traditional attire encouraged. No outside food.

title: Marine Corps Marathon 2026 — The People's Marathon
description: The third-largest US marathon and world's largest with no prize money. Run past DC's monuments with Marines cheering you on.
long_description: Known as 'The People's Marathon,' the Marine Corps Marathon is the third-largest marathon in the US and the world's largest without prize money. The 51st edition takes runners on a spectacular tour of Washington DC — past the Pentagon, along the Potomac, through Georgetown, around the National Mall, and past the Capitol. US Marines manage every mile, handing out hydration, cheering runners on, and placing finisher medals. The emotional 'wear blue: run to remember' mile honors fallen service members. Registration opens April 6.
venue_info: Start: Pentagon parking lot, Arlington, VA. Finish: Marine Corps War Memorial (Iwo Jima). Metro (Pentagon station, Blue/Yellow lines) is the best way to get there. Health & Fitness Expo at the National Building Museum. 6-hour time limit.

title: TCS New York City Marathon 2026
description: The world's largest marathon with 60,000+ runners through all five NYC boroughs. A bucket-list race celebrating its 50th anniversary course.
long_description: The TCS New York City Marathon is the world's largest marathon and one of the six World Marathon Majors. Over 60,000 runners from 130+ countries cross the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge and run through all five boroughs — Staten Island, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, and Manhattan — before the iconic Central Park finish. The 2026 edition marks the 50th anniversary of the five-borough course. Two million spectators line the streets, making it arguably the most electrifying marathon atmosphere on Earth. The race has raised over $600 million for charity since 2006.
venue_info: Start: Fort Wadsworth, Staten Island (ferry/bus transport from Manhattan). Finish: Central Park, near Tavern on the Green. Subway serves the finish area (B/C to 72nd St). Entry is by lottery, charity, or guaranteed qualifier. 59,226 finishers in 2025.

title: Diwali Festival — Hindu Temple of Greater Chicago
description: Diwali celebrations at one of the largest Hindu temples in the Midwest with puja, fireworks, and cultural show.
long_description: The Hindu Temple of Greater Chicago in Lemont hosts its annual Diwali celebration, one of the Midwest's biggest. The evening features Lakshmi Puja, a grand cultural program, community dinner, and fireworks. The temple's stunning Rajasthani architecture creates a magical setting for the Festival of Lights.

title: Diwali at BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham — Robbinsville, NJ
description: Diwali at the largest Hindu temple in the US — spectacular lighting, cultural programs, and community celebrations.
long_description: Experience Diwali at the magnificent BAPS Akshardham in Robbinsville, NJ — the largest Hindu temple in the Western hemisphere. The campus transforms with thousands of lights, rangoli, and diyas. Features devotional programs, cultural performances, fireworks, and a community dinner. An awe-inspiring setting for the Festival of Lights.
venue_info: 112 N Main St, Robbinsville, NJ. Massive parking facility. Free registration required for weekend visits. Campus closed Tuesdays. Modest dress code required.

title: Diwali Festival — Shiva Vishnu Temple Livermore
description: Grand Diwali celebration at Livermore's Shiva Vishnu Temple with Lakshmi Puja, fireworks, and community feast.
long_description: The Shiva Vishnu Temple's Diwali celebration is one of the Bay Area's most attended Hindu festivals. The day-long program includes Lakshmi Puja, special abhishekams, cultural performances, and a community feast. The temple grounds are illuminated with thousands of diyas and festive lighting. A must-attend for Bay Area families.
venue_info: 1232 Arrowhead Ave, Livermore. All-day event. Expect very large crowds — shuttle service often provided from overflow parking. Prasadam and festival food available.

title: Diwali Celebrations — Sri Venkateswara Temple, Pittsburgh
description: Diwali at America's oldest traditional Hindu temple with Lakshmi Puja and grand celebrations.
long_description: Celebrate Diwali at the historic Sri Venkateswara Temple in Penn Hills — the first traditional Hindu temple in America. Special Lakshmi Puja, Sahasranama archana, cultural performances, and fireworks make this one of Pittsburgh's most significant Hindu celebrations.
venue_info: 1230 S McCully Dr, Penn Hills, PA 15235. All-day event. Free parking. Prasadam and festival food.

venue_info: 3818 212th St SE, Bothell, WA 98021. Free parking. All-day event. Prasadam served.

title: Diwali Celebrations — BAPS Mandir, Los Angeles
description: Grand Diwali at BAPS Los Angeles with traditional pujas, cultural performances, and fireworks.
long_description: Celebrate Diwali at the stunning BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Chino Hills. The temple's pink sandstone and white marble architecture shines brilliantly when illuminated for Diwali. Programs include Lakshmi Puja, Chopda Puja for business owners, cultural shows, and spectacular fireworks. One of LA's most attended Hindu celebrations.
venue_info: 15100 Fairfield Ranch Rd, Chino Hills, CA 91709. Free parking. Open 9 AM–7:30 PM. Prasadam served.

description: Grand Diwali at the Boston area's Sri Lakshmi Temple with Lakshmi Puja and cultural programs.

venue_info: 117 Waverly St, Ashland, MA 01721. All-day event. Ample parking. Prasadam and festival food.

title: Diwali Celebrations — Sri Meenakshi Temple, Houston
description: Houston's beloved Sri Meenakshi Temple celebrates Diwali with Lakshmi Puja, fireworks, and community feast.
long_description: Sri Meenakshi Temple in Pearland hosts Houston's premier temple Diwali celebration. The grand evening features elaborate Lakshmi Puja, thousands of diyas, cultural programs, a fireworks display, and community dinner. The temple's impressive Dravidian architecture provides a stunning backdrop for the Festival of Lights.
venue_info: 17130 McLean Rd, Pearland, TX. Free parking. Large grounds accommodate thousands of visitors.

title: Diwali Festival — DFW Hindu Temple, Irving
description: Grand Diwali celebration at the DFW Hindu Temple with Lakshmi Puja, fireworks, and cultural programs.
long_description: The DFW Hindu Temple's Diwali is the Dallas area's biggest Hindu celebration. Features Lakshmi Puja, cultural performances, children's programs, food stalls, and an evening fireworks display. Thousands of families gather for this annual festival of lights.
venue_info: 1605 N Britain Rd, Irving, TX 75061. All-day event. Shuttle from overflow parking on busy days.

title: Diwali Festival — Malibu Hindu Temple
description: Diwali at the iconic Malibu Hindu Temple with Lakshmi Puja, fireworks, and panoramic mountain views.

long_description: Celebrate Diwali at one of Southern California's most scenic temples. The Malibu Hindu Temple's Diwali program features Lakshmi Puja, special abhishekams, cultural performances, and the spectacular sight of diyas lit against the Santa Monica Mountains backdrop. A unique and unforgettable Diwali experience in the LA area.
venue_info: 1600 Las Virgenes Canyon Rd, Calabasas. All-day event. Parking fills up fast — arrive early. Prasadam available.

title: Diwali Celebrations — BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Milpitas
description: Grand Diwali celebration at the BAPS Mandir with lighting ceremony, cultural program, and community feast.
long_description: BAPS Milpitas hosts its spectacular Diwali celebration, the Festival of Lights. The evening features thousands of diyas illuminating the mandir, a cultural program with devotional performances, fireworks, and a community dinner. One of the most visually stunning Diwali celebrations in the Bay Area.
venue_info: BAPS Mandir, Milpitas. Large parking facility. Expect heavy crowds — arrive early. Modest dress code required inside the mandir.

title: Diwali Mela — BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir Houston

long_description: BAPS Houston celebrates Diwali with a grand mela featuring the traditional lighting of diyas, rangoli competition, cultural performances by youth and adults, and a spectacular fireworks display. The community dinner serves traditional Gujarati and Indian festive sweets. A cherished annual tradition for Houston's Indian community.
venue_info: BAPS Mandir, Houston. Large parking lot. Family-friendly. Modest dress code inside the mandir.

title: Diwali Mela — Sunnyvale Hindu Temple
description: Annual Diwali Mela at Sunnyvale Hindu Temple with Lakshmi Puja, fireworks, and cultural performances.

Festive food stalls offer traditional sweets and savories. One of the Bay Area's most well-attended Diwali celebrations.
venue_info: 450 Persian Drive, Sunnyvale. Free parking. Expect heavy crowds — arrive early for best parking. Dress in festive attire.

long_description: Bharatiya Temple's Diwali celebration is the highlight of the Detroit-area Hindu community's calendar. venue_info: 6850 Adams Rd, Troy, MI 48098. All-day event with parking on-site. Festival food vendors. Dress festively!

venue_info: 3033 N Hayden Rd, Scottsdale, AZ 85251. Free parking. Open 10 AM–9 PM on Diwali. Prasadam and festival food available.

The temple grounds are illuminated with diyas and festive decorations.
venue_info: 6905 Cipriano Rd, Lanham, MD 20706. All-day event. Shuttle service from overflow parking. Traditional dress encouraged.

description: Dallas's premier marathon weekend with full marathon, half, ultra, 5K, and relay options. Benefits Scottish Rite for Children.

The race weekend features a full marathon, half marathon, ultra marathon, 5-person relay, 10K, and 5K — something for every runner. The course starts at Dallas City Hall, loops through scenic White Rock Lake, and finishes back downtown. Since 1997, the marathon has donated nearly $5 million to Scottish Rite for Children. The December timing provides cool running weather, and the event has sold out three consecutive years.
venue_info: Start/finish at Dallas City Hall, 1500 Marilla St. The course is flat and fast, passing through downtown Dallas and around White Rock Lake (120m total elevation gain). DART light rail serves the City Hall area. Post-race party with food, beer, and live music.
